book_name: 英语综合教程(修订版)学生用书第二册

words.ex: He is a handsome boy.
words.ex_cn: 他是个英俊的男孩。
words.en: A handsome man is good-looking, usually in a way that is attractive to women. Something that is handsome is large in quantity or impressive in quality.

words.tr: n. 影响；效果；效应；作用；“effect”的复数；
words.ex: The effects of pollution are harmful to animals.
words.ex_cn: 污染对动物有有害的影响。
words.en: Effects refer to the results or consequences of an action or other cause.

words.tr:
v. 奉承；讨好
adj. 更平坦的；更扁平的；“flat”的比较级
adv. 更平直地；更直截了当地；“flat”的比较级
words.ex: He flatters his boss to get a raise.
words.ex_cn: 他奉承老板以获得加薪。
words.en: If someone flatters you, they praise you in an exaggerated way that may be sincere or may be intended to persuade you to do something.

words.tr: phrase. 自鸣得意；自以为是；自欺地认为
words.ex: He likes to flatter himself by saying he is the best player on the team.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢自夸说他是队里最棒的球员。
words.en: If you flatter yourself that something good is true about you, you believe it about yourself, perhaps wrongly.

words.tr:
adj. 疲倦的；厌烦的
v. （使）厌倦；厌烦
words.ex: He looked weary after working all day.
words.ex_cn: 他工作了一整天后看起来很疲惫。
words.en: If you are weary, you are very tired.

words.ex: She wore a beautiful gown to the wedding.
words.ex_cn: 她穿了一件漂亮的礼服去参加婚礼。
words.en: A gown is a long, loose piece of clothing worn on formal occasions or by people in particular professions.

words.ex: I couldn't apprehend the math lesson because it was too fast.
words.ex_cn: 我无法理解这节数学课，因为讲得太快了。
words.en: If the police apprehend someone, they catch them and arrest them.

words.tr: v. 吞食；吞噬；狼吞虎咽地吃；如饥似渴地看
words.ex: The dog devoured the meat quickly.
words.ex_cn: 狗很快地把肉吃光了。
words.en: To eat something quickly and eagerly, especially because you are very hungry; to destroy something quickly and completely.

words.ex: He hastened to finish his homework before dinner.
words.ex_cn: 他赶紧在晚饭前写完作业。
words.en: If you hasten to do something, you quickly do it or quickly go somewhere.

words.ex: The artist interweaves colors to make a beautiful pattern.
words.ex_cn: 艺术家将颜色交织在一起，创造出美丽的图案。
words.en: To interweave means to weave or blend together two or more things so that they cannot be separated easily.

words.ex: Behold the beautiful sunset.
words.ex_cn: 看那美丽的日落。
words.en: To see or observe (someone or something, especially something remarkable or impressive).

words.ex: She beseeched him to stay with her.
words.ex_cn: 她恳求他留下来陪她。
words.en: If you beseech someone to do something, you ask them very eagerly and anxiously.

words.ex: The rain gave us a short respite from the heat.
words.ex_cn: 这场雨为我们带来了短暂的凉爽缓解。
words.en: A respite is a short period of rest or relief from something difficult or unpleasant.

words.tr: n. 卧室; （君主的）侍寝官
words.ex: She retired to her bedchamber to rest.
words.ex_cn: 她回到卧室休息。
words.en: A bedchamber is a room where a bed is kept, especially in a large or old house.

words.tr: v. 杀死；杀害；残害；宰杀
words.ex: He slayed the monster in the dark forest.
words.ex_cn: 他在黑暗的森林里杀死了怪物。
words.en: To kill someone or something in a violent way.

words.tr: n. 女主人；情妇；女教师（英）
words.ex: The mistress of the house welcomed the guests warmly.
words.ex_cn: 女主人热情地欢迎了客人。
words.en: A woman who has control or authority over others, especially a woman who is in charge of a household or institution.

words.tr:
n. 努力争取；出价；投标；
v. 出价；投标；
words.ex: His bid for the championship inspired everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他为冠军所做的努力鼓舞了所有人。
words.en: To bid means to offer a particular amount of money for something that is being sold, especially at an auction, or to offer to do work or provide services for a particular price.

words.ex: The treacherous road made driving very scary.
words.ex_cn: 这条危险的道路让驾驶非常可怕。
words.en: If you describe someone as treacherous, you mean that they are likely to betray you and cannot be trusted. If you say that something is treacherous, you mean that it is very dangerous and unpredictable.

words.tr: n. （名词）畸形状态：遭致变形后的状态
words.ex: The accident caused a deformity in his leg.
words.ex_cn: 事故导致他的腿变形。
words.en: A deformity is a part of someone's body that is not the normal shape because of injury, illness, or because they were born that way.

words.tr:
v. 害怕；畏惧
n. 恐惧；畏惧
words.ex: He dreads going to the dentist.
words.ex_cn: 他害怕去看牙医。
words.en: If you dread something, you fear it intensely.

words.ex: He asked for her consent before starting the project.
words.ex_cn: 他在开始这个项目之前征求了她的同意。
words.en: Consent is permission for something to happen or agreement to do something.

words.ex: He earned the esteem of his colleagues through hard work.
words.ex_cn: 他通过努力工作赢得了同事们的尊重。
words.en: If you esteem someone or something, you respect or admire them.

words.tr:
n. 脸红；羞愧
v. 泛红；羞愧
words.ex: He felt shy and got a blush when she praised him.
words.ex_cn: 当他被她夸奖时，他感到害羞，脸红了。
words.en: If you blush, your face turns red because you are embarrassed or ashamed.

words.ex: The pine grows tall in the forest.
words.ex_cn: 松树在森林里长得很高。
words.en: A pine is a type of evergreen tree which has long thin leaves called needles and produces cones. As a verb, to pine means to feel a deep longing or desire for something or someone.

words.ex: He frets about his exam results.
words.ex_cn: 他为考试成绩感到烦躁不安。
words.en: If you fret about something, you worry about it.

words.tr:
v. 同意；赞成
n. 同意；赞成
words.ex: He gave his assent to the plan.
words.ex_cn: 他同意了这个计划。
words.en: If you assent to something, you agree to it or agree with it.

words.ex: The disease afflicted many people in the village.
words.ex_cn: 这种疾病使村子里许多人遭受痛苦。
words.en: If you are afflicted by pain, illness, or misfortune, it causes you great suffering and distress.

words.ex: Her smile has a special charm.
words.ex_cn: 她的微笑有一种特别的魅力。
words.en: If you say that someone has charm, you mean that they behave in a friendly and pleasant way that makes people like them. A charm is also a small ornament that is fixed to a bracelet or necklace.

words.ex: The boy resembles his father.
words.ex_cn: 这个男孩长得像他父亲。
words.en: If one thing or person resembles another, they are similar to each other.

words.tr:
n. 棚屋；简陋的小屋
v. 居住
words.ex: He lives in a small shack near the lake.
words.ex_cn: 他住在湖边的一间小木屋里。
words.en: A shack is a small, simple building, often made of wood or metal, which is not very well built or comfortable.

words.ex: The furry cat curled up on the sofa.
words.ex_cn: 那只毛茸茸的猫蜷缩在沙发上。
words.en: Covered with or resembling fur.

words.tr:
v. 咕哝；（猪等）打呼噜
n. 咕哝；呼噜声
words.ex: He grunted when he lifted the heavy box.
words.ex_cn: 他搬起沉重的箱子时咕哝了一声。
words.en: To make a low, short guttural sound, typically to express dissatisfaction or effort.

words.tr:
n. 打巴掌
v. 用巴掌打
adv. 恰好地；猛地
words.ex: He gave the table a loud smack.
words.ex_cn: 他重重地拍了一下桌子。
words.en: If you smack someone or something, you hit them with your open hand. It can also refer to the sound made by a quick, sharp blow or the taste or flavor of something.

words.tr:
n. 嘘声；不满之声
v. 发嘘声
words.ex: The audience started catcalling when the speaker made a controversial statement.
words.ex_cn: 当演讲者发表有争议的言论时，观众开始发出嘘声。
words.en: A catcall is a loud whistle or a comment shouted by someone in a crowd, usually expressing disapproval or mockery.

words.ex: He eats a nut every morning for breakfast.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上吃一颗坚果当早餐。
words.en: A nut is a fruit consisting of a hard or tough shell around an edible kernel. It is also a metal block with a threaded hole that is used with a bolt to fasten things together. Informally, it can refer to someone who is crazy or eccentric.

words.tr:
adj. 红了脸的；兴奋的；激动的
v. 冲洗；脸红；冲（抽水马桶）；“flush”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: She felt her cheeks grow flushed with embarrassment.
words.ex_cn: 她感到自己的脸因尴尬而涨红。
words.en: If someone is flushed, their face is red because they are hot, excited, or embarrassed.

words.ex: He sat astride the fence.
words.ex_cn: 他跨坐在围栏上。
words.en: If you sit or stand astride something, you have one leg on each side of it.

words.tr:
adj. 弯曲的；扭曲的；欺诈的；不老实的
v. （使）弯曲；使成钩状；“crook”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: The path was crooked and hard to walk on.
words.ex_cn: 这条路是弯曲的，很难走。
words.en: If you describe something as crooked, especially something that is usually straight, you mean that it is bent or twisted.

words.ex: The yak is grazing on the mountain.
words.ex_cn: 牦牛正在山上吃草。
words.en: A yak is a large domesticated wild ox with shaggy hair, humped shoulders, and large horns, used in Tibet as a pack animal and for its milk, meat, and hide.

words.ex: The bird made a soft chirp in the morning.
words.ex_cn: 鸟儿在早晨发出轻柔的唧唧声。
words.en: If a bird or an insect chirps, it makes short high-pitched sounds.

words.tr:
n. 等价物；
adj. 相等的；等价的；
words.ex: The dollar is the equivalent of ten yuan.
words.ex_cn: 美元是十元的等价物。
words.en: If one amount or value is the equivalent of another, they are the same.

words.tr:
v. 奔驰；飞奔
n. 奔驰；飞奔
words.ex: The horse gallops across the field.
words.ex_cn: 马在田野上疾驰。
words.en: If a horse gallops, it runs very fast so that all four legs are off the ground at the same time in each stride.

words.ex: The knight rode his steed into battle.
words.ex_cn: 骑士骑着他的战马冲向战场。
words.en: A steed is a horse that is ridden, especially a spirited one for state of war or parade.

words.ex: The frog hopped over the stone.
words.ex_cn: 青蛙跃过了那块石头。
words.en: To move by jumping on one foot or to move quickly and lightly from one place to another.

words.ex: The gallant soldier saved his comrades in battle.
words.ex_cn: 这位英勇的士兵在战斗中救了他的战友们。
words.en: If someone is gallant, they behave bravely and honorably in a dangerous or difficult situation. It can also describe someone who is very polite and kind towards women.

words.tr:
n. （马等动物的）蹄
v.  走；步行；以蹄踢（踏）
words.ex: The horse stepped on the rock with its hoof.
words.ex_cn: 马用蹄子踩在石头上。
words.en: The horny part of the foot of an ungulate animal, especially a horse.

words.ex: The company's profits quadrupled last year.
words.ex_cn: 公司去年的利润增长了四倍。
words.en: To quadruple something means to make it four times as great in size, amount, or number.

words.tr: n. 软帽；汽车发动机罩；阀帽
words.ex: The girl wore a white bonnet to the church.
words.ex_cn: 这个女孩戴着一顶白色软帽去教堂。
words.en: A bonnet is a type of hat that is tied under the chin and was traditionally worn by women and girls. It can also refer to the metal cover over the engine of a car.

words.ex: The old woman was rumored to be a hag who cursed the village.
words.ex_cn: 这位老妇人被谣传是一个诅咒村庄的女巫。
words.en: An old woman considered to be ugly or frightening; a witch.

words.tr:
v. 大口吞咽；喘气；抑制
n. 一大口；吞咽
words.ex: He gulped down his water quickly.
words.ex_cn: 他迅速地吞下了水。
words.en: If you gulp something, you eat or drink it very quickly by swallowing large quantities of it at once.

words.tr: adj. 枯萎的，被害的，被诅咒的 v. （用炸药）炸毁( blast的过去式和过去分词 ); 狠打
words.ex: The blasted tree had been struck by lightning.
words.ex_cn: 那棵枯萎的树被闪电击中了。
words.en: Used to express annoyance or anger.

words.ex: He has a wart on his hand.
words.ex_cn: 他手上有一个疣。
words.en: A wart is a small, hard, benign growth on the skin, caused by a virus.

words.ex: My throat is sore after singing.
words.ex_cn: 我唱歌后喉咙疼。
words.en: If part of your body is sore, it causes you pain and discomfort.

words.ex: He drank water from a cup.
words.ex_cn: 他从杯子里喝水。
words.en: A cup is a small round container that you drink from. Cups usually have handles and are made from china or plastic.

words.ex: She dresses stylishly every day.
words.ex_cn: 她每天都穿得很时尚。
words.en: In a manner that is fashionable or elegant.

words.ex: He parked his car on the driveway.
words.ex_cn: 他把车停在了车道上。
words.en: A driveway is a private road that leads from a public road to a house or other building.

words.tr: adj. 愚蠢的；空洞的；无意义的
words.ex: His inane comments made everyone bored.
words.ex_cn: 他无聊的评论让每个人都感到无聊。
words.en: If you describe someone's comments or ideas as inane, you mean they are very silly or stupid.

words.ex: The recipe is perfect for beginners.
words.ex_cn: 这个食谱对初学者来说是完备的。
words.en: Something that is perfect is as good as it could possibly be.

words.tr: n. （大车）车轮; 侧手翻，侧身筋斗
words.ex: The old cart had a broken cartwheel.
words.ex_cn: 这辆旧马车的一个车轮坏了。
words.en: A cartwheel is a fast, skillful movement in which you turn your body sideways, place your hands on the ground, and bring your legs over your head in a circular motion. It can also refer to the large, circular wheels of a cart.

words.ex: The boy did a backflip off the trampoline.
words.ex_cn: 男孩从蹦床上做了个后空翻。
words.en: A backward somersault performed in the air.

words.tr: v. 设计舞蹈动作；编舞
words.ex: She choreograph the dance for the school play.
words.ex_cn: 她为学校的戏剧设计了舞蹈动作。
words.en: To choreograph is to compose the sequence of steps and movements for a dance or a ballet.

words.ex: The children were playing on the swingset in the park.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在公园的秋千组合上玩耍。
words.en: A swingset is a structure with swings attached to it, typically found in playgrounds for children to play on.

words.ex: The loud noise exasperates me.
words.ex_cn: 巨大的噪音让我感到烦躁。
words.en: If someone or something exasperates you, they annoy you and make you feel frustrated or impatient.

words.tr: adj. 狂乱无秩序的；喧闹的；难控制的
words.ex: The rambunctious children were causing chaos in the classroom.
words.ex_cn: 喧闹的孩子们在教室里制造混乱。
words.en: If you describe someone, especially a child, as rambunctious, you mean that they are full of energy and difficult to control.

words.ex: She is a petite girl with big eyes.
words.ex_cn: 她是一个眼睛很大的娇小女孩。
words.en: If you describe a woman as petite, you are politely saying that she is small and slim.

words.tr:
n. 雀斑；小斑点
v. （使）生雀斑
words.ex: He has freckles on his nose.
words.ex_cn: 他的鼻子上有雀斑。
words.en: A freckle is a small, brownish spot on the skin, often becoming more pronounced through exposure to the sun.

words.tr:
adj. 凉爽的；酷的；凉的；顶好的；
v. 变凉；
words.ex: The water is cool after the rain.
words.ex_cn: 雨后水很凉爽。
words.en: If you say that a person or their behavior is cool, you mean that they are calm and unemotional, especially in a difficult situation.

words.ex: He is a lanky boy who plays basketball.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个瘦高个男孩，打篮球。
words.en: If you describe someone as lanky, you mean that they are tall and thin and move awkwardly.

words.ex: The ferocious wind knocked down the tree.
words.ex_cn: 强烈的风把树吹倒了。
words.en: A ferocious animal or person is very fierce and violent.

words.tr: adv. 愉快地；欣喜地；幸灾乐祸地
words.ex: The children danced gleefully in the rain.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在雨中欢快地跳舞。
words.en: If you say that someone does something gleefully, you mean that they do it with great pleasure and enjoyment, often because they think it will upset or annoy someone else.

words.tr: n. 回路；环行；电路；巡回；
words.ex: The battery connects to the circuit to make the light work.
words.ex_cn: 电池连接到回路，使灯亮起来。
words.en: A circuit is a roughly circular line, route, or movement that starts and finishes at the same place. It can also refer to the complete path that an electric current travels along.

words.tr: v. 要求归还；收回；开垦；感化
words.ex: He wants to reclaim his lost wallet.
words.ex_cn: 他想要要求归还他丢失的钱包。
words.en: If you reclaim something that you have lost or that has been taken away from you, you succeed in getting it back. If you reclaim land, you make it suitable for use, for example by draining it or by getting rid of unwanted buildings or plants.

words.ex: The company made a subdivision of its market by age.
words.ex_cn: 公司按年龄对市场进行了细分。
words.en: A subdivision is a part or section of something which is itself divided into parts.

words.tr:
v. 把…塞进狭窄的空间；把…藏入
n. 褶皱；零食
words.ex: He tucked the letter into his pocket.
words.ex_cn: 他把信塞进了口袋里。
words.en: If you tuck something somewhere, you put it there so that it is safe, comfortable, or neat.

words.ex: The old wall began to crumble after the rain.
words.ex_cn: 旧墙在雨后开始坍塌。
words.en: If something crumbles, or if you crumble it, it breaks into a lot of small pieces.

words.ex: Good teachers motivate students to learn.
words.ex_cn: 好老师激励学生学习。
words.en: To motivate someone means to provide them with a reason for doing something, especially something that requires effort.

words.ex: He excels in math.
words.ex_cn: 他擅长数学。
words.en: To be exceptionally good at or proficient in an activity or subject.

words.ex: He tried to instigate a fight at the party.
words.ex_cn: 他试图在聚会上挑起争斗。
words.en: If someone instigates an event or situation, they cause it to happen by their actions or behavior.

words.ex: The children love watching animated movies.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们喜欢看动画电影。
words.en: Animated means full of life or excitement, or made to appear to move as if by magic or technology.

words.tr: n. 拼贴画；拼贴艺术；杂烩
words.ex: He made a collage from old magazine pictures.
words.ex_cn: 他用旧杂志的图片做了一幅拼贴画。
words.en: A collage is a picture that has been made by sticking pieces of colored paper, cloth, or photographs onto a surface.

words.tr: n. 正式舞会，毕业舞会
words.ex: He wore a suit to the prom.
words.ex_cn: 他穿西装去参加毕业舞会。
words.en: A prom is a formal dance held for a high school or college class, typically at the end of the academic year.

words.ex: He bought a flower in remembrance of his mother.
words.ex_cn: 他买了一朵花以纪念他的母亲。
words.en: The act of remembering something or someone, or a memory of someone or something.

words.tr: adj. 招致不满的；不公平的；难以决定的
words.ex: He made an invidious comparison between his two students.
words.ex_cn: 他对他的两个学生做了令人不快的比较。
words.en: If you describe a task or job as invidious, you mean that it is likely to make you unpopular because it is unpleasant or difficult to do.

words.tr:
v. 轻弹；轻击；轻拂；忽然摇动
n. 轻弹；轻拂；快速的轻打
words.ex: He flicked the light switch on.
words.ex_cn: 他 flick 了一下电灯开关。
words.en: To move or hit something with a quick, sharp movement.

words.tr: n. 大型废弃物；巨大笨重的人（物）
words.ex: The old boat was left as a hulk on the shore.
words.ex_cn: 那艘旧船被遗弃在岸边，成为了一堆大型废弃物。
words.en: A hulk is a large, clumsy, or old ship that is no longer in use and is often left to decay in a harbor.

words.ex: There was a dip in sales last month.
words.ex_cn: 上个月销售额有所下降。
words.en: To dip something means to put it into a liquid and then take it out again.

words.ex: He is my confidant and I tell him everything.
words.ex_cn: 他是我的知己，我什么都告诉他。
words.en: A confidant is someone you can share your secrets with or discuss personal matters with, knowing that they will keep your information private.

words.ex: He bought a gift for his spouse.
words.ex_cn: 他给他的配偶买了一份礼物。
words.en: A spouse is a person's partner in marriage.

words.ex: The taxonomist meticulously categorized the specimens.
words.ex_cn: 分类学者一丝不苟地对标本进行了分类。
words.en: A taxonomist is a scientist who specializes in the classification of organisms into groups on the basis of their structure, origin, behavior, etc.

words.tr: n. 扑灭的人，害虫驱除剂
words.ex: The exterminator was called to remove the infestation of termites.
words.ex_cn: 灭虫员被叫来清除白蚁的侵扰。
words.en: An exterminator is a person whose job is to kill insects, rats, etc. that are considered pests.

words.ex: The colors in the rainbow cover a wide spectrum.
words.ex_cn: 彩虹中的颜色覆盖了广泛的范围。
words.en: A spectrum is a range of a particular type of thing, often a range of colors, ideas, or opinions.

words.tr: n. 需优先考虑的事；优先权；
words.ex: Homework is my top priority.
words.ex_cn: 作业是我最需要优先考虑的事。
words.en: If something is a priority, it is the most important thing you have to do or deal with, or must be done or dealt with before everything else you have to do.

words.tr: n. 诅咒；受诅咒的事；逐出教门；十分讨厌的人（或事物）
words.ex: Lying is anathema to her.
words.ex_cn: 说谎是她所诅咒的。
words.en: Something or someone that one vehemently dislikes.

words.tr: n. 神经症；神经衰弱症
words.ex: He has a neurosis about being late.
words.ex_cn: 他对迟到有一种神经症般的焦虑。
words.en: A neurosis is a mental illness that causes feelings of fear and worry, often leading to unreasonable behavior.

words.ex: The sweater shrinks in hot water.
words.ex_cn: 这件毛衣在热水中会收缩。
words.en: If something shrinks or you shrink it, it becomes smaller.

words.ex: His smile gave me reassurance.
words.ex_cn: 他的微笑让我安心。
words.en: If someone needs reassurance, they are very worried and need someone to help them stop worrying by saying kind or helpful things.

words.ex: He is constantly checking his phone.
words.ex_cn: 他不断地查看他的手机。
words.en: If something happens constantly, it happens all the time or very often.

words.ex: The bright lights caused stimulation in her eyes.
words.ex_cn: 明亮的灯光引起了她眼睛的刺激。
words.en: The act of arousing or accelerating physiological or psychological activity or response in an organism or any of its parts.

words.ex: He resisted the temptation to eat cake.
words.ex_cn: 他抵制了吃蛋糕的诱惑。
words.en: If you feel you want to do something or have something, even though you know you really should avoid it, you can refer to this feeling as temptation.

words.tr: adj. 先已存在的；早已存在的
words.ex: The injury was pre-existing before the accident.
words.ex_cn: 这次事故前伤势已经存在。
words.en: Existing before something else.

words.tr: n. 连撞两球，连击 vi. <美>碰击弹回，一击连撞二球，碰击而反跳
words.ex: He attempted a carom shot, but missed both balls.
words.ex_cn: 他尝试了一次连撞两球的击球，但两个球都没碰到。
words.en: To hit something and bounce off at an angle.

words.ex: He knows good etiquette at dinner.
words.ex_cn: 他知道晚餐时的礼貌规矩。
words.en: Etiquette refers to the customary code of polite behavior in society or among members of a particular profession or group.

words.ex: His rude behavior alienated his friends.
words.ex_cn: 他粗鲁的行为使朋友们疏远了他。
words.en: To cause someone to feel isolated or estranged; to transfer the ownership of property to another.

words.ex: The law constrains companies from polluting rivers.
words.ex_cn: 法律约束公司不得污染河流。
words.en: To constrain someone or something means to limit their development or force them to behave in a particular way.

words.tr: phrase. 激起某人的情绪或热情；鼓动某人行动
words.ex: The coach whipped the team up before the big game.
words.ex_cn: 教练在大赛前激励了球队。
words.en: To whip someone up means to stir them into action or to excite them, often emotionally.

words.tr: phrase. 快速制作或准备某物；迅速召集或组织某事物
words.ex: She managed to whip up a delicious meal in no time.
words.ex_cn: 她很快就做好了一顿美味的饭菜。
words.en: To prepare or make something, especially food, very quickly.

words.tr:
v. （使）回旋；（使）旋转
n. 一连串的事；混乱；尝试
words.ex: The wind makes the leaves whirl around.
words.ex_cn: 风让树叶旋转飞舞。
words.en: To move or cause to move rapidly around and around.

words.ex: He eats gourmet food at a fancy restaurant.
words.ex_cn: 他在一家高档餐厅吃精致美食。
words.en: A gourmet is someone who knows a lot about food and cooking, and who enjoys eating high-quality food.

words.tr:
n. 垫；爪垫；便笺簿
v. 放轻脚步走
words.ex: She put a pad on the chair for comfort.
words.ex_cn: 她在椅子上放了一个垫子以增加舒适感。
words.en: A pad is a flat piece of material that is used to protect something, to make something more comfortable, or to absorb liquid.

words.ex: The sun was dazzlingly bright at noon.
words.ex_cn: 中午时分，阳光耀眼明亮。
words.en: In a manner that is extremely bright, impressive, or skillful.

words.ex: He looked furtively around before taking the cookie.
words.ex_cn: 他拿饼干前偷偷地看了看四周。
words.en: If you do something furtively, you do it in a way that shows you want to keep it secret or hidden, often because it is wrong or you are ashamed.

words.tr:
n. 变种；变体
v. 改变；变化
words.ex: This butterfly has a rare morph with blue wings.
words.ex_cn: 这种蝴蝶有一种罕见的蓝色翅膀变种。
words.en: To morph means to change smoothly from one image to another by small gradual steps using computer animation techniques.

words.tr:
v. 拍动；摆动；
n. 薄片；
words.ex: The bird flaps its wings to fly.
words.ex_cn: 鸟拍动翅膀飞翔。
words.en: A flap is a piece of cloth, paper, skin etc that is fixed at one edge to a surface, which you can lift up easily. If something such as a piece of cloth or paper flaps or if you flap it, it moves quickly up and down or from side to side.

words.tr: n. 醉心工作，迷恋工作
words.ex: Workaholism can lead to burnout and health problems.
words.ex_cn: 醉心工作可能导致倦怠和健康问题。
words.en: Workaholism is the compulsion or the strong desire to work excessively hard and long hours.

words.tr: adj. 引起幽闭恐怖的；（患）幽闭恐怖症的
words.ex: The small elevator made him feel claustrophobic.
words.ex_cn: 这个小电梯让他感到幽闭恐怖。
words.en: If you feel claustrophobic, you feel very uncomfortable or anxious when you are in a small, crowded, or enclosed place.

words.tr: adj. 有微风的；轻松愉快的
words.ex: The park was breezy and full of people enjoying the weather.
words.ex_cn: 公园里微风习习，到处都是享受天气的人们。
words.en: If you describe something as breezy, you mean that it is light, informal, and cheerful.

words.tr: n. 性受虐狂者；受虐狂者
words.ex: He revealed himself to be a masochist, enjoying the pain inflicted on him.
words.ex_cn: 他透露自己是一个受虐狂，喜欢别人施加在他身上的痛苦。
words.en: A masochist is someone who enjoys receiving pain or humiliation, especially in a sexual context.

words.ex: He lives in a quiet borough of New York.
words.ex_cn: 他住在纽约的一个安静的行政区。
words.en: A borough is a town, or a district within a large city, that has its own local government.

words.ex: Smartphones supplanted landline phones.
words.ex_cn: 智能手机取代了固定电话。
words.en: To supplant someone or something means to take the place of them, often by being more powerful or effective.

words.tr: n. 闯入者；干涉他人事务者
words.ex: The interloper walked into the meeting without permission.
words.ex_cn: 那个闯入者未经允许走进了会议。
words.en: An interloper is someone who becomes involved in a situation or place where they are not wanted or are considered not to belong.

words.tr:
n. 鞭策；
v. 刺激；
words.ex: The competition served as a spur to work harder.
words.ex_cn: 竞争成了推动他更努力工作的鞭策。
words.en: A spur is something that makes you want to do something or that encourages you to do it. It can also refer to a sharp device worn on the heel of a rider's boot to urge a horse forward.

words.ex: He admitted his infidelity after the argument.
words.ex_cn: 他在争吵后承认了自己的不忠行为。
words.en: Infidelity refers to the action or state of being unfaithful to a spouse or other sexual partner.

words.tr: n.不值得保存的; (尤指在战斗中)为达某种目的而可牺牲的物品(如容易补充的军需、给养、装备等)或人员(
words.ex: The concept of expendability in warfare is controversial.
words.ex_cn: 在战争中关于可牺牲性的概念是有争议的。
words.en: The quality of being expendable, that is, able to be sacrificed or used up in order to achieve an objective.

words.ex: The confrontation between the two teams was intense.
words.ex_cn: 两队之间的对抗非常激烈。
words.en: A confrontation is a situation in which there is a lot of disagreement or argument about something important.

words.ex: He flung his hat on the chair.
words.ex_cn: 他把帽子扔在椅子上。
words.en: To throw something quickly and carelessly; to move or do something suddenly and energetically.

chapters.name: Unit 3 Money and Happiness Text A

words.ex: The class analyzed statistical data from the survey.
words.ex_cn: 这个班级分析了调查的统计数据。
words.en: Relating to the use of statistics or statistical methods.

words.ex: The price of bread went up because of inflation.
words.ex_cn: 由于通货膨胀，面包的价格上涨了。
words.en: Inflation is a general increase in prices and fall in the purchasing value of money.

words.ex: The designer created a new dress for the show.
words.ex_cn: 这位设计师为这场秀设计了一条新裙子。
words.en: A designer is a person who plans the form, structure, or appearance of something before it is made, by preparing drawings or plans.

words.ex: The teacher showed a chart of temperatures.
words.ex_cn: 老师展示了一张温度图表。
words.en: A chart is a graphical representation of data, in which the data is represented by symbols, such as bars in a bar chart, lines in a line chart, or slices in a pie chart.

words.ex: The incidence of flu increased last winter.
words.ex_cn: 去年冬天流感的发生率上升了。
words.en: The incidence of something is the frequency with which it occurs or the rate at which it happens.

words.tr: v. 使衰弱；使虚弱；“debilitate”的现在分词；
words.ex: The illness was debilitating her strength.
words.ex_cn: 这场疾病正在使她的体力衰弱。
words.en: If you say that a disease or condition is debilitating, you mean that it makes people physically or mentally weak.

words.tr: v. 使发出刺耳声，发出叮当声；刺激，烦扰；争论；闲聊; n. 争吵，吵嚷；刺耳声，金属撞击声；闲聊
words.ex: The keys jangled in his pocket.
words.ex_cn: 钥匙在他的口袋里叮当作响。
words.en: If objects jangle, or if you jangle them, they make a loud, harsh noise as they move or are moved.

words.tr: phrase. 经历…而幸存；度过（艰难时期）；经受住
words.ex: He lived through a big storm last year.
words.ex_cn: 他去年经历了一场大风暴。
words.en: To experience and survive a difficult or dangerous situation.

words.ex: Dark clouds are a predictor of rain.
words.ex_cn: 乌云是下雨的预示物。
words.en: A predictor is someone or something that makes it possible for you to say what will happen or how someone will behave in the future.

words.ex: The rain rendered the road slippery.
words.ex_cn: 雨水使道路变得滑溜。
words.en: To render something means to cause it to become or to provide it. It can also mean to express or translate something.

words.ex: The relentless rain flooded the streets.
words.ex_cn: 无情的雨水淹没了街道。
words.en: Someone who is relentless is determined to do something and refuses to give up, even if what they are doing is unpleasant or cruel.

words.ex: The system can decouple the two parts to work separately.
words.ex_cn: 这个系统可以将两个部分分离，以便分别工作。
words.en: To disconnect or separate something from something else, especially to stop one thing from being influenced by another.

words.ex: The scientist tried to replicate the experiment.
words.ex_cn: 这位科学家试图复制这个实验。
words.en: To replicate something means to do or make something again in exactly the same way.

words.tr: 短语动词. 有道理；说得对
words.ex: You have a point about saving money.
words.ex_cn: 你关于存钱的说法有道理。
words.en: If someone has a point, what they say is reasonable or correct, especially when they are disagreeing with you.

words.tr:
n. 中位数；（三角形的）中线
adj. 中间值的；中间的
words.ex: The median of 3, 5, and 7 is 5.
words.ex_cn: 3、5和7的中位数是5。
words.en: The median is the middle number in a sorted, ascending or descending, list of numbers and can be more descriptive of that data set than the average.

words.ex: The university has great prestige for its research.
words.ex_cn: 这所大学因其研究而享有很高的声望。
words.en: The widespread respect and admiration felt for someone or something on the basis of a perception of their achievements or quality.

words.ex: The university conferred an honorary degree on him.
words.ex_cn: 大学授予他一个荣誉学位。
words.en: To confer something such as a degree or an honor on someone means to give it to them in a formal way. To confer with someone means to discuss something with them in order to make a decision.

words.tr: phrase. 过奢侈的生活；大手大脚地花钱；生活优渥
words.ex: After winning the lottery, they started to live high on the hog.
words.ex_cn: 中彩票后，他们开始过上了奢华的生活。
words.en: To live in a very luxurious or extravagant manner.

words.tr: n. （有共同特点或举止类同的）一群人；一批人；
words.ex: The cohort of students all started college in 2020.
words.ex_cn: 这群学生都是在2020年进入大学的。
words.en: A cohort is a group of people who share a common characteristic or experience.

words.ex: The speaker will amplify the sound for everyone to hear.
words.ex_cn: 扬声器会放大声音，让每个人都能听到。
words.en: To amplify something means to make it louder, stronger, or more detailed.

words.tr:
adv. 极其地
adj. 异常巨大的；非常重要的
words.ex: They launched a mega marketing campaign.
words.ex_cn: 他们启动了一场宏大的营销活动。
words.en: extremely large or great

words.tr: n. 因循守旧; 陈旧古板的做法; 前后紧接; 步伐一致
words.ex: The company's lockstep approach to innovation stifled creativity.
words.ex_cn: 公司因循守旧的创新方式扼杀了创造力。
words.en: A mode of marching in step by a body of persons going abreast.

words.tr: adj. 抬高的；地位高的； v. “elevate”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The walkway is elevated above the road.
words.ex_cn: 这条人行道被抬高在道路之上。
words.en: An elevated place or thing is higher than the area around it.

words.tr:
n. 住所；居住处
v. 逗留；“abide”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: His abode is a small house near the lake.
words.ex_cn: 他的住所是一栋靠近湖边的小房子。
words.en: A place of residence; a home.

words.tr: v. 告诉；讲述；“tell”的现在分词； adj. 有力的；反映情况的；
words.ex: He told me the news.
words.ex_cn: 他告诉了我这个消息。
words.en: If something is telling, it shows the true nature of a situation or someone's feelings or character in a very clear way.

words.ex: His condition improved after the treatment.
words.ex_cn: 他的状况在接受治疗后好转了。
words.en: A condition is a state of affairs that must exist or be brought about before something else can happen or be done.

words.ex: There are a lot of books on the shelf.
words.ex_cn: 书架上有许多书。
words.en: A lot refers to a large number or amount of something. It can also mean a piece of land or someone's fate or destiny.

words.ex: I anticipate rain tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 我预料明天会下雨。
words.en: If you anticipate an event, you realize in advance that it may happen and you are prepared for it.

words.ex: He wore a decent shirt to the interview.
words.ex_cn: 他穿了一件像样的衬衫去面试。
words.en: Decent is used to describe something which is considered to be of an acceptable standard or quality.

words.tr: adj. 被许可的； v. “license”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: He is a licensed doctor.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位有执照的医生。
words.en: Officially permitted or authorized to do something.

words.tr: adv. 自相矛盾地；矛盾地；
words.ex: Paradoxically, he is very quiet, but he speaks the most in class.
words.ex_cn: 自相矛盾地，他非常安静，但在课堂上却说得最多。
words.en: In a way that is contrary to expectations or seemingly contradictory.

words.ex: His speech impediment made it hard for him to talk clearly.
words.ex_cn: 他的口吃使他难以清晰地说话。
words.en: An impediment is something that makes it difficult to do or achieve something.

words.tr: adj. （对某人[某事物]）固恋，异常依恋 v. 注视; 视线移向( fixate的过去式和过去分
words.ex: She became increasingly fixated on the idea of traveling to Japan.
words.ex_cn: 她越来越执迷于去日本旅行的想法。
words.en: If someone is fixated on a particular thing, they think about it a lot and find it difficult to think about anything else.

words.ex: The police discovered a scheme to steal money.
words.ex_cn: 警方发现了一个偷钱的阴谋。
words.en: A scheme is a plan or arrangement, especially one produced by a government or other organization, or a secret plan to do something, especially something illegal or dishonest.

words.tr: adj. 赤贫的；贫困的；一无所有的；
words.ex: The destitute family had no food or shelter.
words.ex_cn: 这个赤贫的家庭没有食物和住所。
words.en: If you describe someone as destitute, you mean they have absolutely nothing, especially no money.

words.tr: adj. 完全的；荒凉的；光秃秃的；僵硬的；严厉的
words.ex: There was a stark difference between the two results.
words.ex_cn: 这两个结果之间有完全的差异。
words.en: Stark means complete, severe, or obvious in a way that is impossible to avoid noticing.

chapters.name: Unit 3 Money and Happiness Text B

words.tr: adj. 不足的；欠缺的；微小的；
words.ex: There is scant evidence to support the claim.
words.ex_cn: 支持这一说法的证据不足。
words.en: If you describe something as scant, you mean that there is not enough of it or that it is not as much as it should be.

words.tr: n. 神经病学家；神经科专门医师
words.ex: The neurologist checked his brain with a machine.
words.ex_cn: 神经科医生用机器检查了他的大脑。
words.en: A neurologist is a doctor who specializes in the study and treatment of disorders of the nervous system.

words.ex: The dark clouds are a harbinger of storm.
words.ex_cn: 乌云是暴风雨的预兆。
words.en: A harbinger is something that shows that something is going to happen soon, especially something bad.

words.tr: n. 精神治疗医师；心理治疗师
words.ex: The psychotherapist helps people feel better.
words.ex_cn: 心理治疗师帮助人们感觉更好。
words.en: A psychotherapist is a person who treats mental illness by using psychological methods rather than medical means.

words.tr:
n. 旋转；
v. 旋转；
words.ex: The spin of the top made it stay upright.
words.ex_cn: 陀螺的旋转让它保持直立。
words.en: If something spins or if you spin it, it turns quickly around a central point.

words.ex: The computer uses a buffer to store data temporarily.
words.ex_cn: 计算机使用缓冲区临时存储数据。
words.en: A buffer is something that prevents something else from being harmed or that reduces the impact of something.

words.ex: He volunteers for civic projects in his town.
words.ex_cn: 他为家乡的市民项目做志愿者。
words.en: Relating to a city or town, especially its administration; relating to the duties or activities of people in relation to their town, city, or local area.

words.tr: adj. 有免疫力的；免疫的；不受影响的；
words.ex: Children are immune to this disease after vaccination.
words.ex_cn: 儿童接种疫苗后对这种疾病有免疫力。
words.en: If you are immune to a particular disease, you cannot be affected by it. If you are immune to something such as criticism, it does not affect you.

words.ex: He will initiate a new project next week.
words.ex_cn: 他将在下周发起一个新项目。
words.en: To initiate something means to start it or cause it to happen.

words.ex: His absenteeism caused the team to lose points.
words.ex_cn: 他的缺勤导致团队丢了分数。
words.en: Absenteeism is the habitual non-presence of an employee at their job.

words.ex: The old adage says, 'Slow and steady wins the race.'
words.ex_cn: 这句古老的格言说：'慢而稳者胜。'
words.en: An adage is a short, wise saying which has been used for a long time and is generally accepted as true.

words.ex: He did a preliminary test before the main experiment.
words.ex_cn: 他在主要实验之前做了一个初步测试。
words.en: Preliminary means something that is done or happens before the main part or event, especially as an introduction or preparation.

words.tr: adj. 引起兴趣的；引人入胜的； v. “intrigue”的现在分词；
words.ex: The mystery story was intriguing.
words.ex_cn: 这个侦探故事很引人入胜。
words.en: If you describe something as intriguing, you mean that it is interesting or strange.

words.ex: He is learning neurobiology at university.
words.ex_cn: 他正在大学学习神经生物学。
words.en: The branch of biology that deals with the anatomy, physiology, and pathology of the nervous system.

words.ex: I perceive a change in his mood.
words.ex_cn: 我察觉到他的情绪有变化。
words.en: If you perceive something, you see, notice, or realize it, especially when it is not obvious.

words.tr: adj. 短暂的；朝生暮死的
words.ex: The flowers are ephemeral and last only one day.
words.ex_cn: 这些花是短暂的，只持续一天。
words.en: Something that is ephemeral lasts for only a very short time.

words.ex: He inherited a house from his father.
words.ex_cn: 他从父亲那里继承了一所房子。
words.en: If you inherit something such as a trait, characteristic, or quality, you are born with it, because your parents or ancestors had it. If you inherit money or property, you receive it from someone who has died.

words.ex: The plasticity of the clay made it ideal for sculpting.
words.ex_cn: 黏土的可塑性使其非常适合雕塑。
words.en: The quality of being easily shaped or molded.

words.ex: His fear of heights is hard-wired from birth.
words.ex_cn: 他对高度的恐惧是与生俱来的。
words.en: If something is hard-wired into a computer or machine, it is built into it and cannot be changed. If a quality or way of behaving is hard-wired into a person or animal, it is a natural part of them that they cannot change.

words.tr: n. 中风；划水动作；一击；
words.ex: He had a stroke last year.
words.ex_cn: 他去年中风了。
words.en: A stroke is a medical condition in which poor blood flow to the brain results in cell death. It can also refer to an act of hitting or striking someone or something, or a gentle movement of the hand over a surface.

words.tr:
adj. 交替的；轮流的；间隔的；
v. （使）交替；（使）轮流；
words.ex: We take alternate days off work.
words.ex_cn: 我们隔天休息一次。
words.en: If something alternates between two things, it repeatedly changes from one to the other and back again.

words.tr: v. 减到最少；使最小化；
words.ex: Try to minimize waste in the kitchen.
words.ex_cn: 尽量减少厨房里的浪费。
words.en: To minimize something means to reduce it to the smallest possible amount or degree.

words.ex: The teacher gave a cue to start the game.
words.ex_cn: 老师给出了开始游戏的提示。
words.en: A cue is a signal for someone to do something, or a piece of information that helps someone to understand something.

words.ex: He ate a ripe persimmon for breakfast.
words.ex_cn: 他早餐吃了一个熟透的柿子。
words.en: A persimmon is a soft, orange fruit that is sweet when ripe and grows on a tree.

words.tr: n. 遗传学家；遗传学工作者；
words.ex: The geneticist studied how traits are passed from parents to children.
words.ex_cn: 这位遗传学家研究了性状是如何从父母传给孩子的。
words.en: A geneticist is a biologist who studies genetics, the science of genes, heredity, and variation of organisms.

words.tr: n. 美食家；讲究饮食的人
words.ex: He is an epicure who loves fine food.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个热爱美食的享乐者。
words.en: An epicure is a person who enjoys high-quality food and drink and is very knowledgeable about it.

words.tr:
n. 流动；
v. 漂移；
words.ex: The drift of the river carries leaves downstream.
words.ex_cn: 河流的流动将树叶冲向下游。
words.en: If something or someone drifts somewhere, they move there slowly or gradually. As a noun, drift can refer to a slow, gradual movement or change, or the general meaning or intent of something.

words.tr: adj. 像食人鱼一样的；凶猛的
words.ex: The company's aggressive marketing strategy is piranha-like, quickly devouring competitors.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司凶猛的营销策略像食人鱼一样，迅速吞噬了竞争对手。
words.en: Resembling or characteristic of a piranha, especially in being aggressive or voracious.

words.ex: The bonus is an incentive to work harder.
words.ex_cn: 奖金是努力工作的动机。
words.en: Something that encourages a person to do something or to work harder.

words.tr: adj. 可疑的；有问题的；不可靠的；
words.ex: The deal seemed questionable.
words.ex_cn: 这笔交易看起来可疑。
words.en: If you say that something is questionable, you mean that it is not obviously true or real, and therefore possibly not valid or reliable.

words.tr: adj. 强制性的；义务的；必须的；
words.ex: Wearing a helmet is obligatory for cyclists.
words.ex_cn: 骑自行车时戴头盔是强制性的。
words.en: If something is obligatory, you must do it because of a rule or law.

words.tr: adj. 很长的；漫长的；冗长的；
words.ex: The meeting was lengthy and tiring.
words.ex_cn: 会议很长，很累人。
words.en: Something that is lengthy lasts for a long time, often longer than you want or expect.

words.tr: adj. 可疑的；怀疑的；拿不准的；
words.ex: The deal seemed dubious to me.
words.ex_cn: 这个交易在我看来很可疑。
words.en: If you describe something as dubious, you mean that you do not consider it to be completely honest, safe, or reliable.

words.ex: The teacher used pedagogical methods to help students learn.
words.ex_cn: 这位老师使用了教育学的方法来帮助学生学习。
words.en: Relating to the methods and theory of teaching.

words.ex: His sensitivity to loud noises makes him wear earplugs.
words.ex_cn: 他对噪音的敏感性让他戴耳塞。
words.en: Sensitivity is the quality or condition of being sensitive—the capacity to respond to slight changes, signals, or influences.

words.ex: He imparts knowledge to his students every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天向学生传授知识。
words.en: If you impart information to people, you tell it to them. To impart a particular quality to something means to give it that quality.

words.ex: The swamp is full of tall grass and frogs.
words.ex_cn: 这个沼泽里长满了高草和青蛙。
words.en: A swamp is an area of low-lying, uncultivated ground where water collects; a bog or marsh.

words.ex: He is a competent teacher who helps students easily.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位有能力的老师，能轻松帮助学生。
words.en: If you are competent to do something, you have the skills, abilities, or experience necessary to do it well.

words.tr: adj.[法] 未经证明的，无证明书的
words.ex: The uncertified documents were not accepted for legal purposes.
words.ex_cn: 未经证明的文件在法律用途上未被接受。
words.en: Not officially recognized as meeting certain standards or requirements.

words.ex: There are innumerable stars in the night sky.
words.ex_cn: 夜空中有数不清的星星。
words.en: Too many to be counted; very many.

words.ex: The fallen tree impeded the car's path.
words.ex_cn: 倒下的树阻碍了汽车的前进。
words.en: To impede something means to make its movement, development, or progress difficult.

words.tr:
adj. 成拱形的；包罗万象的；支配一切的；首要的
v. 在上方成拱形；“overarch”的现在分词
words.ex: The bridge has an overarching shape.
words.ex_cn: 这座桥有一个成拱形的形状。
words.en: Most important, because it includes or affects all other things.

words.ex: His recipe for success is hard work and patience.
words.ex_cn: 他成功的秘诀是努力工作和耐心。
words.en: A recipe is a list of ingredients and a set of instructions that tell you how to cook something.

words.tr: v. 使平等；使均等；使相等
words.ex: The law aims to equalize opportunities for all people.
words.ex_cn: 法律旨在使所有人机会平等。
words.en: To make things equal in amount, size, or value.

words.tr: v. 射击；拍摄（电影）；疾驰；“shoot”的过去式和过去分词； n. 照片；射击；射门；
words.ex: He shot the target with his gun.
words.ex_cn: 他用枪射击了目标。
words.en: A shot is an act of shooting a gun, or the sound that this makes. It can also refer to an attempt to do something, a photograph, or an injection.

words.tr:
v. 促进；使增长；
n. 提高；增强；
words.ex: Exercise can boost your energy.
words.ex_cn: 锻炼可以促进你的精力。
words.en: If one thing boosts another, it causes it to increase, improve, or be more successful.

words.ex: The city became prosperous after the new factory opened.
words.ex_cn: 新工厂开业后，这座城市变得繁荣了。
words.en: A prosperous person, place, or economy is rich and successful.

words.tr: adj. 豪华的；昂贵时髦的
words.ex: The ritzy hotel was filled with wealthy guests.
words.ex_cn: 这家豪华的酒店里住满了富有的客人。
words.en: If you describe something as ritzy, you mean that it is fashionable and expensive.

words.ex: The king issued an edict to stop the war.
words.ex_cn: 国王发布了一项法令来停止战争。
words.en: An edict is an official order or proclamation issued by a person in authority.

words.tr: adj. 联邦的；联邦制的；联邦政府的；
words.ex: The federal government passed a new law.
words.ex_cn: 联邦政府通过了一项新法律。
words.en: A federal system of government is one in which there is a central government and separate governments for each of the states or regions.

words.tr:
n. 鞋带；小额资本
adj. 小本经营的
words.ex: He tied his shoestring before running.
words.ex_cn: 他跑步前系好了鞋带。
words.en: A shoestring is a small amount of money that is not enough to pay for much, or a lace used to fasten shoes.

words.ex: He was beset by problems at work.
words.ex_cn: 他被工作中的问题困扰。
words.en: If someone or something is beset by problems or fears, they have many problems or fears which affect them severely.

words.ex: Honesty is an inherent quality of a good leader.
words.ex_cn: 诚实是好领导固有的品质。
words.en: Existing in something as a permanent, essential, or characteristic attribute.

words.ex: The company's revenue increased last year.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司的收入去年增加了。
words.en: Revenue is the income that a company, organization, or government receives regularly.

words.ex: The teacher will distribute the books to students.
words.ex_cn: 老师将把书分发给学生。
words.en: If you distribute things, you hand them or deliver them to a number of people.

words.ex: He contends that education is the key to success.
words.ex_cn: 他主张教育是成功的关键。
words.en: If you contend with someone or contend with something, you have to deal with a difficult situation or problem. If you contend that something is true, you state or argue that it is true.

words.ex: The agency helps people find jobs.
words.ex_cn: 这个机构帮助人们找工作。
words.en: An agency is a business which provides a service on behalf of other businesses.

words.tr: n. 官僚主义；官僚机构
words.ex: He hates the bureaucracy in government offices.
words.ex_cn: 他讨厌政府办公室里的官僚主义。
words.en: Bureaucracy refers to a system of government or business that has many complicated rules and ways of doing things.

words.tr: adj.不能打动人的；无吸引力的
words.ex: The food looked unappealing.
words.ex_cn: 这食物看起来不吸引人。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as unappealing, you mean they are not attractive or interesting.

words.ex: The police confiscate illegal drugs.
words.ex_cn: 警察没收非法毒品。
words.en: If you confiscate something from someone, you take it away from them, usually as a punishment.

words.tr: v. 授权；命名；给...权利（或资格）
words.ex: This book entitles you to a free gift.
words.ex_cn: 这本书使你有资格获得一份免费礼物。
words.en: If you are entitled to something, you have the right to have it or do it.

words.ex: She implored him to stay.
words.ex_cn: 她恳求他留下。
words.en: If you implore someone to do something, you ask them to do it in a forceful, emotional way.

words.ex: He has an appetite for spicy food.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢辛辣食物。
words.en: A desire or liking for something, especially food.

words.tr: adj. 可怜的；悲哀的；差劲的；令人生厌的
words.ex: The little dog looked pathetic in the rain.
words.ex_cn: 那只小狗在雨中看起来很可怜。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as pathetic, you mean that they are sad and weak or inadequate, and you feel contempt or pity for them.

words.tr: n. 庞然大物；怪物；巨兽；
words.ex: The old factory was a monstrosity of rust and steel.
words.ex_cn: 那座旧工厂是一座锈迹斑斑的钢铁庞然大物。
words.en: Something that is very large and extremely ugly, or that is shocking or wrong because it is not natural.

words.tr:
n. 支撑物；支柱；道具
v. 支撑；靠
words.ex: He uses a prop to support the shelf.
words.ex_cn: 他用一个道具来支撑架子。
words.en: A prop is an object or piece of furniture that is used in a play or film to make a scene look more realistic, or something that is used to support or hold up another object.

words.tr: adj. 暴虐的；压制的；残暴的
words.ex: The tyrannical king punished people for small mistakes.
words.ex_cn: 这个暴虐的国王因为小错误惩罚人民。
words.en: Using power in a cruel and unfair way over people in a country or group.

words.ex: The new regime changed the tax laws.
words.ex_cn: 新的管理制度改变了税法。
words.en: A regime is the set of rules or the way that a country or organization is governed, especially when it is considered to be strict or unfair.

words.ex: The farmer feeds the pigs to fatten them.
words.ex_cn: 农夫喂猪使它们长胖。
words.en: To make or become fat or fatter.

words.tr:
prep. 通过；穿过；
adv. 从头到尾地；彻底；
adj. 直通的；
words.ex: He walked through the door.
words.ex_cn: 他穿过了门。
words.en: Moving in one side and out of the other side of (an opening, channel, or location).

words.tr:
n. 提倡者；
v. 提倡；
words.ex: He is an advocate for clean water.
words.ex_cn: 他是清洁用水的提倡者。
words.en: If you advocate a particular action or plan, you recommend it publicly.

words.ex: The survey asks about your gender.
words.ex_cn: 这个调查询问你的性别。
words.en: Gender is the state of being male or female, especially when considered with reference to social and cultural differences, not just biological ones.

words.ex: The superintendent of the school is very strict.
words.ex_cn: 学校的主管非常严格。
words.en: A superintendent is a person who is in charge of a particular department or activity, especially within a school, housing project, or police force.

words.ex: He violated the school rule by using his phone in class.
words.ex_cn: 他上课使用手机，违反了校规。
words.en: If someone violates an agreement, law, or promise, they break it.

words.ex: The amendment changed the old law.
words.ex_cn: 这项修正案改变了旧法律。
words.en: An amendment is a change or addition to a law or document.

words.ex: The hikers faced great peril in the storm.
words.ex_cn: 徒步者在风暴中面临巨大危险。
words.en: Peril refers to serious and immediate danger.

words.ex: The affluent family bought a big house by the lake.
words.ex_cn: 这个富裕的家庭在湖边买了一栋大房子。
words.en: Having a great deal of money; wealthy.

words.tr: adj. 教区的；地方范围的；思想狭隘的
words.ex: The priest served in a small parochial church.
words.ex_cn: 牧师在一座小型教区教堂服务。
words.en: If you describe someone as parochial, you are criticizing them because you think they are too concerned with their own affairs and should be thinking about more important things.

words.ex: The company improved data retention after upgrading its system.
words.ex_cn: 公司在升级系统后提高了数据保留能力。
words.en: The action of retaining something; the continued possession, use, or control of something.

words.ex: The company values flexibility in work hours.
words.ex_cn: 公司重视工作时间的灵活性。
words.en: Flexibility refers to the quality of bending easily without breaking, or the ability to be easily modified to respond to altered circumstances or conditions.

words.ex: The local company is an affiliate of the big global brand.
words.ex_cn: 这家本地公司是这个全球大品牌的分公司。
words.en: If an organization is affiliated with another larger organization, it is officially connected with the larger organization or is a member of it.

words.ex: The two parties formed a coalition to win the election.
words.ex_cn: 这两个政党联合起来以赢得选举。
words.en: A coalition is a temporary alliance for combined action, especially of political parties forming a government.

words.ex: The adverse weather delayed the flight.
words.ex_cn: 不利的天气延误了航班。
words.en: If something is adverse, it is harmful or unfavorable.

words.tr: v. 使（尤指不好的情形、体系、信仰）持续、长存；
words.ex: The system perpetuates inequality among the poor.
words.ex_cn: 这个体系使贫困人群的不平等持续存在。
words.en: To perpetuate something means to cause it to continue, especially for a long time.

words.tr:
n. 刻板印象；陈规老套
v. 对…存有成见；把…模式化
words.ex: He broke the stereotype that boys cannot cry.
words.ex_cn: 他打破了男孩不能哭的刻板印象。
words.en: A stereotype is a fixed general image or set of characteristics that a lot of people believe represent a particular type of person or thing.

words.ex: He solves algebra problems every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天解代数题。
words.en: Algebra is a branch of mathematics in which letters and symbols are used to represent numbers and quantities in formulae and equations.

words.tr: v. （给顾客）少找钱；不公平对待
words.ex: The shopkeeper short-changed me by five dollars.
words.ex_cn: 店主给我少找了五美元。
words.en: To give someone less change than they are owed, especially deliberately.

words.ex: His argument is based on anecdotal evidence.
words.ex_cn: 他的论点基于轶事证据。
words.en: Anecdotal evidence is based on personal accounts rather than on research that can be verified.

words.tr: adj. 令人信服的； v. “compel”的现在分词；
words.ex: His story was compelling and made everyone listen.
words.ex_cn: 他的故事令人信服，让所有人都认真聆听。
words.en: A compelling argument or reason is one that makes you believe it or accept it because it is so strong.

words.ex: He bought a repair kit for his bike.
words.ex_cn: 他买了一套自行车维修工具。
words.en: A kit is a group of items that are kept together, often in the same container, because they are all used for similar purposes.

words.ex: The manager showed accountability for the mistake.
words.ex_cn: 经理对这个错误承担了责任。
words.en: The fact or condition of being accountable; responsibility.

words.ex: They live in a suburban neighborhood near the city.
words.ex_cn: 他们住在靠近城市的市郊社区。
words.en: Suburban means relating to a suburb, which is an area on the edge of a large town or city where people live. It often implies a residential area with a lower population density than the inner city.

words.ex: The physician checked the patient's temperature.
words.ex_cn: 医生检查了病人的体温。
words.en: A physician is a medical doctor who is trained in the diagnosis and treatment of diseases and injuries.

words.tr: adj. 虔诚的；衷心的；诚挚的；
words.ex: He is a devout Christian who goes to church every Sunday.
words.ex_cn: 他是一名虔诚的基督徒，每周日都去教堂。
words.en: If you describe someone as devout, you mean that they have a deep religious faith.

words.tr:
adj. 音乐的；擅长音乐的；
n. 音乐剧；音乐歌舞片；
words.ex: He loves musical songs.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢音乐的歌曲。
words.en: Relating to music; having the pleasant sound of music.

words.ex: Parents should foster good habits in children.
words.ex_cn: 父母应该培养孩子的好习惯。
words.en: To foster something means to encourage and promote its development.

words.tr:
n. （果树的）花朵；
v. 开花；
words.ex: The apple tree is full of blossom in spring.
words.ex_cn: 春天时，苹果树上开满了花。
words.en: When a tree or plant blossoms, it produces flowers before producing fruit that can be eaten.

words.tr:
n. 特征；报刊特写；
v. 以…为特色；是…的重要组成；
words.ex: The main feature of this phone is its long battery life.
words.ex_cn: 这款手机的主要特征是续航时间长。
words.en: A feature of something is an interesting or important part or characteristic of it.

words.ex: He is the protagonist in the story.
words.ex_cn: 他是故事中的主角。
words.en: The main character in a story, play, film, etc., especially the one who is good or who the audience is expected to support.

words.ex: He has a natural aptitude for math.
words.ex_cn: 他天生有数学天赋。
words.en: An aptitude is a natural ability to do something.

words.tr:
n. 合同；契约；
v. 收缩；
words.ex: They signed a contract to buy the house.
words.ex_cn: 他们签署了一份购买房子的合同。
words.en: A contract is a legal agreement between two or more parties. It can also mean to become smaller or tighter, or to catch a disease.

words.ex: He likens his job to a puzzle.
words.ex_cn: 他把他的工作比作一个拼图。
words.en: To liken something to something else is to say that they are similar in some way.

words.tr:
n. (从事某项活动的)规定期限
v. 吝惜；节省
words.ex: He did a short stint as a teacher.
words.ex_cn: 他短暂地当过一段时间老师。
words.en: A stint is a fixed period of time during which someone does a particular job or activity.

words.ex: After a long convalescence, she was finally able to return to work.
words.ex_cn: 经过长时间的恢复期后，她终于能够重返工作岗位。
words.en: Convalescence is the period or process of becoming healthy and strong again after an illness or operation.

words.ex: She bought new decoration for her living room.
words.ex_cn: 她为客厅买了新的装饰品。
words.en: Decoration is the process or art of decorating something, or the objects used to decorate something.

words.ex: The infantry marched through the forest.
words.ex_cn: 步兵穿过森林行进。
words.en: Infantry refers to soldiers who fight on foot, especially in contrast to cavalry or artillery.

words.ex: He practiced stoicism by staying calm during hardship.
words.ex_cn: 他在逆境中保持冷静，践行斯多亚学派的哲学。
words.en: Stoicism is the endurance of pain or hardship without the display of feelings and without complaint.

words.tr:
v. 包括；遮盖；报道；
n. 遮盖物；庇护所；封面；
words.ex: The book covers basic math and science.
words.ex_cn: 这本书包括基础数学和科学。
words.en: If something covers something else, it has been placed over or upon it, usually in order to protect it or hide it.

words.ex: The Greco-Roman style is a blend of Greek and Roman architectural elements.
words.ex_cn: 希腊罗马风格是希腊和罗马建筑元素的融合。
words.en: A prefix meaning 'Greek' or 'Greek-style'.

words.ex: The correspondent reported the news from the city.
words.ex_cn: 记者从城市报道了新闻。
words.en: A correspondent is someone who reports news from a particular place or on a particular subject for a newspaper, magazine, or television or radio station.

words.ex: The stylistic choice of words made the poem more beautiful.
words.ex_cn: 词语的文体选择使这首诗更加优美。
words.en: Relating to the style or manner of something, especially in literature or art.

words.ex: The sun is at its zenith at noon.
words.ex_cn: 太阳在正午时分达到最高点。
words.en: The zenith is the time at which something is most powerful or successful.

words.tr: adj. 死后的；死后出版的；遗腹的
words.ex: He received a posthumous award for his bravery.
words.ex_cn: 他因勇敢而被追授了奖项。
words.en: Posthumous means occurring, awarded, or appearing after the death of the originator.

words.tr:
n. 草图；素描；概述
v. 草拟；速写；简述
words.ex: He made a quick sketch of the house.
words.ex_cn: 他快速画出了房子的草图。
words.en: A sketch is a simple, quickly-made drawing that does not have many details. It can also mean a short description or account of something.

words.tr:
v. 移居国外；把…逐出国外
n. 侨民；移居国外者
adj. 移居国外的；被逐出国外的
words.ex: He decided to expatriate to Canada for a better life.
words.ex_cn: 他决定移居加拿大以追求更好的生活。
words.en: An expatriate is someone who lives in a country that is not their own, often for work or political reasons.

words.ex: Birds inhabit the forest near the lake.
words.ex_cn: 鸟类居住在湖边的森林里。
words.en: If a place or region is inhabited by a group of people or a species of animal, those people or animals live there.

words.tr:
adj. 智力的；
n. 知识分子；
words.ex: He is an intellectual person who loves solving math problems.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个热爱解决数学问题的智力型人。
words.en: An intellectual is someone who spends a lot of time studying and thinking about complicated ideas.

words.tr: v. 使不朽；使永存；使名垂千古
words.ex: The statue will immortalize the hero.
words.ex_cn: 这座雕像将使这位英雄永垂不朽。
words.en: To immortalize someone or something means to make them famous for a very long time, often by creating a work of art or literature about them.

words.ex: The book opens with an epigraph from a famous philosopher.
words.ex_cn: 这本书以一位著名哲学家的题词开篇。
words.en: An epigraph is a short quotation or saying at the beginning of a book or chapter, intended to suggest its theme.

words.ex: Many people decry the use of plastic bags.
words.ex_cn: 许多人公开反对使用塑料袋。
words.en: If you decry something, you criticize it as being wrong or harmful.

words.tr: n. 爱国主义；爱国精神；
words.ex: He showed patriotism by serving his country in the army.
words.ex_cn: 他通过在军队中为国家服务表现出爱国主义。
words.en: Patriotism is the love and devotion to one's country.

words.ex: Honesty is the main tenet of his life.
words.ex_cn: 诚实是他生活的宗旨。
words.en: A tenet is a principle or belief, especially one that is part of a larger system of beliefs.

words.ex: The rain caused a torrent down the mountain.
words.ex_cn: 大雨在山间形成了一股急流。
words.en: A torrent is a fast-moving stream of water or other liquid.

words.tr: v. 承诺；犯（罪、错）；（公开地）表达意见；
words.ex: He commit to help his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他承诺帮助他的朋友。
words.en: To commit means to carry out or perpetrate a mistake, crime, or immoral act; or to pledge or bind oneself to a certain course of action.

words.ex: He has hypertension and takes medicine every day.
words.ex_cn: 他有高血压，每天吃药。
words.en: Hypertension is a condition in which the force of the blood against the artery walls is too high.

words.tr: n. （在非洲的）旅行；狩猎旅行；
words.ex: We went on a safari in Kenya to see lions and elephants.
words.ex_cn: 我们去肯尼亚旅行，去看狮子和大象。
words.en: A safari is a trip to observe or hunt wild animals, especially in East or Southern Africa.

words.ex: The submarine sailed quietly under the sea.
words.ex_cn: 潜水艇在海底安静地航行。
words.en: A submarine is a type of ship that can travel underwater. It is used primarily by the military for defense purposes, but some are used for scientific research.

words.tr: n. 观察机; 监靶员; 测位仪; 检路器
words.ex: The spotter carefully watched the landing aircraft for any signs of trouble.
words.ex_cn: 观察机仔细观察着降落的飞机，寻找任何麻烦的迹象。
words.en: A spotter is someone who watches a particular activity or situation carefully in order to see what happens or to look for something specific.

words.ex: The actor received acclaim for his performance.
words.ex_cn: 这位演员因他的表演而受到赞扬。
words.en: If someone or something is acclaimed, they are praised enthusiastically and publicly.

words.tr: v. 送医院治疗；使住院
words.ex: He was hospitalized after the accident.
words.ex_cn: 他在事故后被送进了医院。
words.en: To admit someone into a hospital for treatment.

words.tr: v. 把…强加给；使遭受；使承受
words.ex: The storm inflicted heavy damage on the village.
words.ex_cn: 风暴给村庄造成了严重破坏。
words.en: If you inflict something unpleasant on someone, you make them suffer it.

words.tr: adj. 艳丽的；炫耀的；神气活现的
words.ex: He wears flamboyant clothes to stand out.
words.ex_cn: 他穿著華麗的衣服來引人注目。
words.en: If you say that someone or something is flamboyant, you mean that they are very noticeable, stylish, and exciting.

words.tr: adj. 遵守纪律的； v. “discipline”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: He is a disciplined student who always arrives on time.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个遵守纪律的学生，总是准时到达。
words.en: Someone who is disciplined behaves in a controlled way, obeying rules or standards.

words.ex: The rebel fought against the king's rules.
words.ex_cn: 这位叛逆者反抗国王的法令。
words.en: A rebel is a person who opposes or fights against people in authority.

words.ex: The cartoon is satirical and makes fun of politicians.
words.ex_cn: 这幅漫画是讽刺性的，嘲笑政客。
words.en: A satirical piece of writing or speech uses satire to criticize people or ideas.

words.ex: He failed the test, but subsequent efforts helped him pass.
words.ex_cn: 他考试没及格，但随后的努力让他通过了。
words.en: Following in time or order; succeeding.

words.ex: The government made a new regulation to control pollution.
words.ex_cn: 政府出台了一项新管理措施来控制污染。
words.en: A regulation is an official rule or order.

words.ex: I bought fresh bread from the bakery.
words.ex_cn: 我从面包房买了新鲜面包。
words.en: A bakery is a place where bread, cakes, and pastries are made or sold.

words.ex: The bombardier dropped the bomb with precision.
words.ex_cn: 投弹手精确地投下了炸弹。
words.en: A bombardier is a member of an aircrew responsible for the aiming and releasing of bombs.

words.ex: He waited in the foyer before the show started.
words.ex_cn: 演出开始前，他在门厅里等候。
words.en: A foyer is an area at the front of a building, especially a hotel or theater, where people can wait or meet others.

words.tr: n. 普通书写（速记或打字）；普通写法
words.ex: He preferred to write in longhand rather than using a typewriter.
words.ex_cn: 他更喜欢手写而不是使用打字机。
words.en: Longhand is a style of writing in which words are written in full, as opposed to being written in shorthand or typed.

words.ex: He writes books under a pseudonym.
words.ex_cn: 他用笔名写书。
words.en: A pseudonym is a name that someone, especially a writer, uses instead of their real name.

words.tr: adj. 预言的；预示的；先知的
words.ex: His words were prophetic when the storm came.
words.ex_cn: 当风暴来临时，他的话应验了。
words.en: If something was prophetic, it described or suggested something that did actually happen later.

words.ex: His repetitious answers made the class bored.
words.ex_cn: 他重复的回答让全班感到无聊。
words.en: Something that is repetitious involves actions or elements that are repeated many times and is therefore boring.

words.tr: adj. 单调乏味的；毫无变化的；
words.ex: The work is monotonous and boring.
words.ex_cn: 这份工作单调乏味。
words.en: Something that is monotonous is very boring because it has a regular, repeated pattern which never changes.

words.tr: adj. 眼花缭乱的；耀眼的； v. “dazzle”的现在分词；
words.ex: The dazzling lights of the city made her blink.
words.ex_cn: 城市的耀眼灯光让她眨了眨眼。
words.en: If you describe something as dazzling, you mean that it is extremely impressive, beautiful, or skilful.

words.ex: The unfair verdict caused public outrage.
words.ex_cn: 不公正的判决引发了公众的愤怒。
words.en: An outrage is an extremely strong reaction of anger, shock, or indignation.

words.ex: The squadron flew over the city at dawn.
words.ex_cn: 中队在黎明时飞过城市。
words.en: A squadron is a principal subdivision of an armored or cavalry regiment, consisting of two or more troops, companies, or batteries.

words.tr: n. 简易机场；临时跑道
words.ex: The small plane landed on the airstrip.
words.ex_cn: 小型飞机降落在飞机跑道上。
words.en: An airstrip is a piece of land that is used by aircraft to take off and land, especially one that is in a remote area and does not have the facilities of an airport.

words.ex: The character is fictitious and does not exist in real life.
words.ex_cn: 这个角色是虚构的，现实中不存在。
words.en: Fictitious means invented and not true or not existing.

words.ex: The conman tricked the old lady into giving him her life savings.
words.ex_cn: 那个骗子骗老太太把她的终身积蓄给了他。
words.en: A conman is a man who persuades people to give him their money or property by lying to them.

words.tr:
n. 脏乱；杂乱；
v. 弄糟；
words.ex: The room was a mess after the party.
words.ex_cn: 派对后房间一片狼藉。
words.en: A mess is a situation that is confused and full of problems, or something that is dirty or untidy.

words.tr: n. 代理；副手；（陆军）中尉；（海军）上尉
words.ex: He acted as lieutenant for the manager while she was away.
words.ex_cn: 当经理离开时，他担任代理。
words.en: A lieutenant is a person who holds a junior officer's rank in the armed forces, or a person who acts as a deputy to a superior.

words.ex: The soldiers assembled on the parade ground for the morning drill.
words.ex_cn: 士兵们在阅兵场上集合进行早操。
words.en: A parade ground is a large open area where soldiers practice marching and where military ceremonies are held.

words.ex: The landlord will evict the tenant for not paying rent.
words.ex_cn: 房东会因为租客不付房租而将他驱逐。
words.en: To evict someone means to force them to leave a house or piece of land, usually because they have not paid the rent or have broken the law.

words.tr: n. 心智健全；神志清楚；神智健全
words.ex: The doctors questioned his sanity after the accident.
words.ex_cn: 事故发生后，医生们质疑他的精神是否健全。
words.en: The condition of having a healthy mind and not being mentally ill.

words.tr:
v. 放电；放出；
n. 排放；
words.ex: The battery will discharge if left unused for a long time.
words.ex_cn: 如果长时间不使用，电池会放电。
words.en: If someone is discharged from a hospital, prison, or the armed forces, they are officially allowed to leave, or told that they must leave. If something is discharged from inside a place, it comes out.

words.tr: adj. 疯狂的；精神失常的；精神错乱的
words.ex: He thinks it's insane to drive without a license.
words.ex_cn: 他认为无证驾驶是疯狂的。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as insane, you mean that they are very foolish or crazy.

words.ex: Drugs can relieve pain.
words.ex_cn: 药物可以减轻疼痛。
words.en: To relieve someone or something means to make a problem, pain, or unpleasant feeling less severe or to take it away completely.

words.tr: adj. 荒唐的；荒唐可笑的；
words.ex: It's absurd to wear a coat in summer.
words.ex_cn: 夏天穿外套是荒唐的。
words.en: If you say that something is absurd, you are criticizing it because you think that it is ridiculous or that it does not make sense.

words.ex: His refusal to listen is irrational.
words.ex_cn: 他拒绝倾听是不合理的。
words.en: If you describe someone's feelings and behavior as irrational, you mean they are not based on logical reasons or clear thinking.

words.ex: The camel walks across the desert.
words.ex_cn: 骆驼穿越沙漠。
words.en: A desert is a large area of land that has very little water and very few plants growing on it. Many deserts are covered by sand. If you desert someone or something, you leave them and no longer help or support them.

words.tr: adj. 按时间先后顺序排列的
words.ex: The events are listed in chronological order.
words.ex_cn: 这些事件按时间顺序列出。
words.en: If things are described or shown in chronological order, they are described or shown in the order in which they happened.

words.tr: adj. 成碎片的；片断的； v. “fragment”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The glass became fragmented after it fell.
words.ex_cn: 玻璃掉落后变成了碎片。
words.en: Something that is fragmented is broken into separate parts or pieces, often in a way that is confusing or makes it difficult to understand the whole.

words.tr: adj. 超现实主义的；离奇的；怪诞的
words.ex: The dream was surreal.
words.ex_cn: 这个梦很超现实。
words.en: If you describe something as surreal, you mean that the elements in it are combined in a strange way that you would not normally expect, like in a dream.

words.ex: The painting depicts a quiet village at sunset.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画描绘了一个宁静的村庄在日落时分的景象。
words.en: To depict someone or something means to show or represent them in a work of art such as a drawing or painting.

words.ex: Her rebelliousness often got her into trouble at school.
words.ex_cn: 她的叛逆性经常让她在学校惹上麻烦。
words.en: The quality of being unwilling to obey rules or accept normal standards of behavior, dress, etc.

words.tr:
n. 全体演员；
v. 投掷；扔；投射；
words.ex: The cast of the play performed very well.
words.ex_cn: 这部剧的全体演员表演得非常好。
words.en: To cast something means to throw it forcefully in a particular direction.

words.ex: The absurdity of his excuse made everyone laugh.
words.ex_cn: 他借口的荒谬让大家都笑了。
words.en: The quality or state of being absurd; something that is absurd.

words.ex: The country's militarism was evident in its aggressive foreign policy.
words.ex_cn: 该国的好战精神在其侵略性的外交政策中显而易见。
words.en: Militarism is the belief or desire of a government or people that a country should maintain a strong military capability and be prepared to use it aggressively to defend or promote national interests.

words.ex: He has insomnia and cannot sleep at night.
words.ex_cn: 他有失眠症，晚上睡不着。
words.en: If someone suffers from insomnia, they find it difficult to sleep.

words.tr:
n. 山；
v. 逐渐增加；
words.ex: He climbed the mount early in the morning.
words.ex_cn: 他一大早爬了那座山。
words.en: To mount something means to go up it or to get on it. It can also refer to the act of organizing and beginning something, such as an event or an exhibition.

words.ex: She looked at him cynically and shook her head.
words.ex_cn: 她冷笑着看着他，摇了摇头。
words.en: In a manner that is distrustful of human sincerity or integrity.

words.tr:
n. 冰雹；
v. 把…誉为；
words.ex: The hail broke many car windows.
words.ex_cn: 冰雹打碎了许多汽车窗户。
words.en: Hail is small balls of ice that fall like rain from the sky. It can also mean to call out to someone in order to attract their attention, or to praise someone enthusiastically.

words.tr:
n. 双关语
v. 说双关语
words.ex: He made a bad pun and everyone groaned.
words.ex_cn: 他开了个蹩脚的玩笑，大家都皱起了眉头。
words.en: A pun is a clever and amusing use of a word or phrase with two meanings, or of words with the same sound but different meanings.

words.ex: The story is an allegory about kindness.
words.ex_cn: 这个故事是一个关于善良的寓言。
words.en: An allegory is a story, poem, or picture which can be interpreted to reveal a hidden meaning, typically a moral or political one.

words.ex: The hostile neighbor shouted at us every morning.
words.ex_cn: 那个敌意的邻居每天早上都对我们大喊大叫。
words.en: If you are hostile to another person or an idea, you disagree with them or disapprove of them, often showing this in your behavior.

words.ex: The king was killed in a regicide.
words.ex_cn: 国王在一次弑君事件中被杀。
words.en: The act of killing a king or queen; a person who kills a king or queen.

words.tr: n. 杀父；杀父者；杀父罪
words.ex: The prince committed patricide to take the throne.
words.ex_cn: 王子为了登上王位而杀死了自己的父亲。
words.en: Patricide is the act of killing one's own father.

words.tr: n. 杀害兄弟者；杀兄弟的行为
words.ex: The act of fratricide is considered one of the most heinous crimes.
words.ex_cn: 杀兄弟的行为被认为是最恶劣的罪行之一。
words.en: Fratricide is the act of killing one's brother or sister, or in a military context, the act of killing a fellow soldier.

words.tr: n. 溺婴; 杀婴，杀婴者; 杀孑; 食子
words.ex: The practice of infanticide was common in many ancient societies.
words.ex_cn: 在很多古代社会，杀婴行为很常见。
words.en: Infanticide is the act of killing an infant, often by a parent or caregiver.

words.ex: He was punished for adultery.
words.ex_cn: 他因通奸而受到惩罚。
words.en: Adultery is voluntary sexual intercourse between a married person and someone who is not their spouse.

words.ex: He told the story about incest in the old family.
words.ex_cn: 他讲了那个关于家族乱伦的旧事。
words.en: Incest is sexual activity between family members or close relatives.

words.tr: n. 斩首; 杀头; 断头术; 大辟
words.ex: The decapitation of the king shocked the entire nation.
words.ex_cn: 国王的斩首震惊了整个国家。
words.en: The action of cutting off the head of a person or animal; the removal of a leader or government from power.

words.ex: He needs rest for recuperation after the surgery.
words.ex_cn: 手术后他需要休息来恢复。
words.en: The process of getting back your health or strength after you have been ill or injured.

words.ex: The movie had a sequel that came out last year.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影有一部去年上映的续集。
words.en: A sequel is a book, film, or play that continues the story of a previous one.

words.ex: The painting is an evocation of the artist's childhood memories.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画唤起了艺术家对童年的回忆。
words.en: The act of bringing or recalling a feeling, memory, or image to the mind.

words.tr:
v. 细述；叙述
n. 叙述；重新计票
words.ex: He tried to recount the accident to the police.
words.ex_cn: 他试图向警察重新叙述那场事故。
words.en: To recount means to tell someone about something that happened, often in detail; or to count something again to make sure the number is correct.

words.ex: He tosses the ball to his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他把球扔给他的朋友。
words.en: To throw something, especially something light, with a quick, light motion.

words.ex: He is clumsy and dropped the glass.
words.ex_cn: 他很笨拙，把玻璃杯打翻了。
words.en: A clumsy person moves or handles things in a careless, awkward way, often so that things are knocked over or broken.

words.ex: He put the papers in a red folder.
words.ex_cn: 他把文件放进了一个红色的活页夹。
words.en: A folder is a thin piece of cardboard or plastic in which you can keep loose papers.

chapters.name: Unit 6 Reflections on Life Text A

words.tr: n. 避难所；庇护所；庇护；
words.ex: The birds found sanctuary in the forest.
words.ex_cn: 这些鸟在森林里找到了避难所。
words.en: A sanctuary is a place where people or animals are protected from danger or trouble.

words.tr: v. 考虑；深思；凝视；思考…的可能性
words.ex: He contemplates quitting his job.
words.ex_cn: 他正在考虑辞去工作。
words.en: If you contemplate an action, you think about whether to do it or not.

words.tr:
n. 同事；（组织的）会员；家伙；同胞；
adj. 同类的；同事的；
words.ex: He works as a fellow with Dr. Smith in the lab.
words.ex_cn: 他在实验室里与史密斯博士一起工作，是他的同事。
words.en: A fellow is a man or boy. In British English, a fellow is also a member of certain academic societies.

words.tr: adj. 烦恼的； v. “distress”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: She looked distressed after hearing the bad news.
words.ex_cn: 听到坏消息后，她显得很烦恼。
words.en: If someone is distressed, they are extremely upset.

words.ex: The travelers found an oasis with water and trees.
words.ex_cn: 旅行者们发现了一个有水和树木的绿洲。
words.en: An oasis is a small area in a desert where water and plants are found, making it a place of relief and beauty in an otherwise barren landscape.

words.tr: adv. 慈祥地；优雅地；优裕地
words.ex: She smiled graciously at the child.
words.ex_cn: 她慈祥地对那个孩子微笑了。
words.en: In a manner that is characterized by charm, good taste, and generosity of spirit.

words.ex: She put a cushion on the chair to make it comfortable.
words.ex_cn: 她在椅子上放了一个靠垫，让它更舒服。
words.en: A cushion is a soft bag of some ornamental material, stuffed with wool, hair, feathers, polyester staple fiber, non-woven material, or even paper torn into fragments. It may be used for sitting or kneeling upon, or to soften the hardness or angularity of a chair or couch.

words.ex: He passed the test, albeit with a low score.
words.ex_cn: 他通过了考试，尽管分数很低。
words.en: You use albeit to introduce a fact or comment which reduces the force or significance of what you have just said.

words.ex: He felt uneasy when he heard the strange noise.
words.ex_cn: 当他听到奇怪的声音时，他感到不安。
words.en: If you are uneasy, you feel anxious, afraid, or embarrassed, because you think that something is wrong or that there is danger.

words.tr:
v. 叹息；叹气
n. 叹息；叹气
words.ex: He sighed when he saw the messy room.
words.ex_cn: 他看到凌乱的房间时叹了口气。
words.en: To sigh is to let out a deep breath slowly and audibly, often as a sign of sadness, tiredness, or relief.

words.tr: adj. 不再抱幻想的； v. “disillusion”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: He became disillusioned after seeing the truth.
words.ex_cn: 在看到真相后，他不再抱幻想了。
words.en: If you are disillusioned with something, you are disappointed because it is not as good as you had expected.

words.tr: phrase. 尽自己的本分；做好分内工作；承担应尽的责任
words.ex: Everyone in the team must pull their weight to finish the project.
words.ex_cn: 团队中的每个人都必须尽自己的责任来完成项目。
words.en: To do one's fair share of work or responsibility in a group or team.

words.tr:
n. 火花；火星；
v. 激发；
words.ex: The match produced a small spark.
words.ex_cn: 火柴产生了一个小火花。
words.en: A spark is a small fiery particle thrown off from a fire, alight in ashes, or produced by striking together two hard surfaces such as stone or metal.

words.tr: n. 替代选择；替代选择（alternative 的复数）；
words.ex: We need to find better alternatives to plastic.
words.ex_cn: 我们需要找到比塑料更好的替代选择。
words.en: An alternative is something that you can choose to do or use instead of something else.

words.ex: We had dinner on the patio.
words.ex_cn: 我们在庭院里吃了晚饭。
words.en: A patio is an outdoor space generally used for dining or recreation that adjoins a residence and is typically paved.

words.ex: It is evident that he is tired.
words.ex_cn: 很明显他很累。
words.en: If something is evident, it is easy to see, perceive, or understand.

words.tr:
v. 力劝；
n. 强烈欲望；
words.ex: My teacher urged me to study harder.
words.ex_cn: 我的老师力劝我更加努力学习。
words.en: If you urge someone to do something, you try hard to persuade them to do it.

words.ex: He will fix the broken chair tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他明天会修理那把坏掉的椅子。
words.en: To fix something means to repair it, to make it firm or stable, or to arrange or decide it.

words.ex: From my standpoint, this plan is too risky.
words.ex_cn: 从我的立场来看，这个计划太冒险了。
words.en: A standpoint is a particular way of considering something, or a particular attitude towards it.

words.ex: There is a tendency for people to use phones before bed.
words.ex_cn: 人们在睡觉前使用手机是一种趋势。
words.en: A tendency is a likelihood of behaving in a particular way or going in a particular direction, which is often bad or undesirable.

words.ex: Running a business entails hard work.
words.ex_cn: 经营企业必然需要努力工作。
words.en: If one thing entails another, it involves it or causes it.

words.ex: The school needs more resources for students.
words.ex_cn: 学校需要为学生提供更多的资源。
words.en: Resources are materials, money, and other assets that can be used to function effectively.

words.tr: phrase. 行走的定时炸弹；比喻潜藏巨大危险、随时可能爆发的人或事物
words.ex: He was a walking time bomb, ready to explode at any moment.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个潜在的危险人物，随时可能爆发。
words.en: A person or thing that is likely to cause a disaster or problem at any time.

words.ex: The bomb will explode at noon.
words.ex_cn: 炸弹将在中午爆炸。
words.en: If an object explodes, it bursts loudly and with great force, often causing damage or injury.

words.ex: He took out a mortgage to buy his first house.
words.ex_cn: 他申请了一笔抵押贷款来购买他的第一套房子。
