words.en: A mortgage is a loan of money which you get from a bank or building society in order to buy a house.

words.ex: The tuition for this course is $500.
words.ex_cn: 这门课程的学费是500美元。
words.en: Tuition is the fee charged for instruction, especially at a college, university, or private school.

words.tr:
adj. 死的；
n. 死人；
adv. 完全地；
words.ex: The dead bird lay on the ground.
words.ex_cn: 那只死鸟躺在地上。
words.en: No longer alive; deprived of life.

words.ex: They decided to prolong the meeting by one hour.
words.ex_cn: 他们决定将会议延长一小时。
words.en: To prolong something means to make it last longer.

words.ex: The storm will intensify tonight.
words.ex_cn: 风暴今晚会加强。
words.en: To make or become more intense or intensive.

words.ex: The government wants to eradicate poverty.
words.ex_cn: 政府希望消灭贫困。
words.en: To eradicate something means to get rid of it completely.

words.ex: His negativity made everyone feel sad.
words.ex_cn: 他的消极情绪让每个人都感到难过。
words.en: The state or character of being negative; the expression of criticism or pessimism.

words.ex: She ate a prune for a healthy snack.
words.ex_cn: 她吃了一颗梅干作为健康零食。
words.en: To prune means to cut off some of the branches of a tree or bush to make it grow better. It can also mean to reduce the extent of something by removing superfluous or unwanted parts.

words.ex: The shrub grows near the fence.
words.ex_cn: 这丛灌木长在篱笆附近。
words.en: A shrub is a woody plant which is smaller than a tree and has several main stems arising at or near the ground.

words.tr: phrase. 闲聊，侃大山，指非正式地长时间聊天
words.ex: They often gather at the corner store to chew the fat.
words.ex_cn: 他们经常在街角商店闲聊。
words.en: To engage in casual conversation or gossip.

words.ex: I went to the park with my buddy.
words.ex_cn: 我和我的同伴去了公园。
words.en: A buddy is a close friend.

words.tr: adj. 传染性的；有感染力的；
words.ex: The flu is contagious and spreads easily.
words.ex_cn: 流感具有传染性，容易传播。
words.en: A contagious disease can be caught by touching someone who has the disease or by touching an infected object or by breathing in infected air.

words.tr:
n. 预算；预算金额；
adj. 廉价的；花钱少的；
v. 为 ... 做预算；
words.ex: We made a budget for our vacation.
words.ex_cn: 我们为旅行制定了一个预算。
words.en: A budget is a plan that shows how much money a person or organization will earn and how much they will need or be able to spend.

words.ex: The rain offset the heat yesterday.
words.ex_cn: 昨天的雨抵消了炎热。
words.en: If one thing is offset by another, the effect of the first thing is reduced by the second, so that any advantage or disadvantage is cancelled out.

words.tr:
n. 纽带；联系；债券；保释金；协定
v. （使）黏合；相互联结
words.ex: Family is the bond that keeps us together.
words.ex_cn: 家庭是我们团结的纽带。
words.en: A bond between people is a strong feeling of friendship, love, or shared beliefs and experiences that unites them.

words.ex: The old man walked with a slow gait.
words.ex_cn: 老人走路步伐缓慢。
words.en: A person's manner of walking.

words.ex: His outlook on life is very positive.
words.ex_cn: 他对生活的观点非常积极。
words.en: Your outlook is your general attitude towards life.

chapters.name: Unit 6 Reflections on Life Text B

words.tr:
v. 引用；报价；
n. 引用；引文；报价；
words.ex: He quoted Shakespeare in his speech.
words.ex_cn: 他在演讲中引用了莎士比亚的话。
words.en: To repeat or copy out (a group of words from a text or speech), typically with an indication that one is not the original author or speaker.

words.ex: The regularity of his daily routine helps him stay focused.
words.ex_cn: 他日常作息的规律性帮助他保持专注。
words.en: The quality or state of being regular; the condition of being governed by or according to rules, principles, or established customs.

words.ex: The smoke came out of the vent.
words.ex_cn: 烟从排气口飘了出来。
words.en: A vent is a hole or opening that allows air, gas, or liquid to pass out of or into a confined space.

words.ex: More often than not, he walks to school.
words.ex_cn: 大多数情况下，他走路去上学。
words.en: If you say that something happens more often than not, you mean that it happens more than half the time.

words.tr:
v. 猛击；重打
n. 猛击；重击；盛会
words.ex: He bashed the door with his fist.
words.ex_cn: 他用拳头猛击门。
words.en: To hit someone or something very hard; a big party or celebration.

words.ex: He turned on the light bulb.
words.ex_cn: 他打开了灯泡。
words.en: A light bulb is an electric lamp which produces light by heating a filament or gas inside a glass bulb.

words.tr: adj. 大胆的；勇敢的； v. “dare”的现在分词；
words.ex: He made a daring jump off the bridge.
words.ex_cn: 他大胆地从桥上跳了下去。
words.en: If you describe a person or their behaviour as daring, you mean that they are willing to do things which might be dangerous or which might shock or anger other people.

words.ex: The view from the mountain is marvelous.
words.ex_cn: 从山上看到的景色极好。
words.en: If you describe something as marvelous, you are emphasizing that it is extremely good.

words.ex: The benefits outweigh the risks.
words.ex_cn: 好处超过了风险。
words.en: If one thing outweighs another, the first thing is of greater importance, benefit, or significance than the second thing.

words.tr:
v. 保证；确保；
n. 保证；保证书；
words.ex: The store guarantees a refund if you are not happy.
words.ex_cn: 如果你不满意，商店保证退款。
words.en: A guarantee is a formal promise that certain conditions will be fulfilled, especially that a product will be repaired or replaced if it is not of a specified quality.

words.tr: adj. 有益的；值得的； v. “reward”的现在分词；
words.ex: Volunteering is a rewarding experience.
words.ex_cn: 志愿服务是一种有益的经历。
words.en: Providing satisfaction or gratification; beneficial.

words.tr:
n. 厄运；毁灭；死亡
v. 注定；判决
words.ex: The old prophecy spoke of doom for the kingdom.
words.ex_cn: 古老的预言说这个王国将遭遇厄运。
words.en: Doom is a terrible fate or destiny that you cannot avoid, especially death or destruction.

words.tr: adj. 殷勤的；顺从的；讨好的
words.ex: He was overly complaisant to his boss, always agreeing with everything he said.
words.ex_cn: 他对老板过于顺从，总是同意他说的每一件事。
words.en: Willing to please others; obliging; agreeable.

words.tr:
n. 研究所；学院；协会；
v. 建立；制定；
words.ex: He works at a research institute.
words.ex_cn: 他在一家研究所工作。
words.en: An institute is an organization set up to do a particular type of work, especially research or teaching. It can also refer to the act of starting something such as a system or an official process.

words.tr: phrase. 与……形成对比；与……对照
words.ex: Her dress contrasts with the white walls.
words.ex_cn: 她的裙子与白墙形成对比。
words.en: To show differences when compared.

words.ex: The norm in this school is to arrive on time.
words.ex_cn: 这所学校的准则就是准时到校。
words.en: A norm is an official standard or level that organizations are expected to reach.

words.ex: He is a renowned scientist.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位有名的科学家。
words.en: Known or talked about by many people; famous.

words.ex: He lives in a small county in the countryside.
words.ex_cn: 他住在乡村的一个小郡里。
words.en: A county is a region of a country used for administrative or other purposes in certain modern nations.

words.ex: He faced persecution for his beliefs.
words.ex_cn: 他因自己的信仰而遭受迫害。
words.en: Persecution is the act of treating someone cruelly or unfairly, especially because of their race, religion, or political beliefs.

words.ex: The emergence of new technology changed our lives.
words.ex_cn: 新技术的出现改变了我们的生活。
words.en: The process of coming into view or becoming exposed after being concealed.

words.ex: Her story inspires me to work harder.
words.ex_cn: 她的故事激励我更加努力。
words.en: If someone or something inspires you to do something new or unusual, they make you want to do it.

words.ex: He dominates the conversation.
words.ex_cn: 他主宰了谈话。
words.en: To dominate means to control or govern someone or something, or to be the most important or noticeable feature of something.

words.tr: adj. 精美的；细腻的；强烈的
words.ex: She wore an exquisite dress to the party.
words.ex_cn: 她穿了一条精美的裙子去参加派对。
words.en: Something that is exquisite is extremely beautiful or pleasant, especially in a delicate or refined way.

words.tr: adj. 现实的；现实主义的；
words.ex: He made a realistic plan to save money.
words.ex_cn: 他制定了一个现实的存钱计划。
words.en: If you are realistic about a situation, you recognize and accept its true nature and try to deal with it in a practical way.

words.tr: n. （基督教的）教牧人员；（任一宗教的）牧师; adj. 牧师的，教士的
words.ex: The cleric delivered a powerful sermon.
words.ex_cn: 这位牧师发表了一篇有力的布道。
words.en: A cleric is a member of the clergy, especially in the Christian Church.

words.tr: adj. 有关联的；相关的；联合的； v. 联想；联合；“associate”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The two events are associated with each other.
words.ex_cn: 这两个事件是有关联的。
words.en: If one thing is associated with another, the two things are connected in some way.

words.tr: adj. 分散的；散落的； v. 散布；分散；“scatter”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The books were scattered on the floor.
words.ex_cn: 书散落在地板上。
words.en: If something is scattered, it is spread out or distributed over a wide area in an irregular way.

words.tr: n. 寄宿处； v. “lodge”的现在分词；
words.ex: He found cheap lodging near the train station.
words.ex_cn: 他在火车站附近找到了便宜的寄宿处。
words.en: Lodging refers to a place to live or stay, especially temporarily.

words.tr:
n. 压力；（动植物的）品种；
v. 竭力；
words.ex: The job gave him a lot of strain.
words.ex_cn: 这份工作给他带来了很大的压力。
words.en: To strain means to make a great effort to do something, to pull or stretch something tightly, or to injure a muscle by stretching it too much.

words.ex: There is friction between the two neighbors over the fence.
words.ex_cn: 两个邻居因为篱笆问题产生了不和。
words.en: The resistance that one surface or object encounters when moving over another.

words.ex: The gownsman presided over the trial with great authority.
words.ex_cn: 这位法官以极大的权威主持了审判。
words.en: A gownsman is a man who wears a gown, especially a member of a university or a lawyer in court.

words.ex: The computer will execute the program quickly.
words.ex_cn: 计算机将快速执行该程序。
words.en: To execute means to carry out or put into effect a plan, order, or course of action. It can also refer to the act of legally killing someone as a punishment.

words.ex: The riot broke out after the game.
words.ex_cn: 比赛结束后爆发了骚乱。
words.en: A riot is a violent disturbance of the peace by a crowd.

words.tr: adj. 首要的；小学的；初等的；原来的；最初的；
words.ex: Primary goal is to stay safe.
words.ex_cn: 首要目标是保持安全。
words.en: Something that is primary is more important than anything else.

words.ex: He worked hard and succeeded in the exam.
words.ex_cn: 他努力学习，考试成功了。
words.en: To achieve something that you have been aiming for, or to take over a position or role after someone else.

words.tr: adj. 值得注意的；显著的；著名的；
words.ex: This is a notable achievement.
words.ex_cn: 这是一个值得注意的成就。
words.en: Worthy of attention or notice; remarkable.

words.ex: The statute says drivers must stop at red lights.
words.ex_cn: 这项法律规定司机必须在红灯时停车。
words.en: A statute is a formal written law of a country or state, enacted by its legislative authority.

words.tr: phrase. 大学的；学院的；与学院有关的 系统
words.ex: The collegiate system ensures that decisions are made collectively.
words.ex_cn: 合议制确保了决策是集体做出的。
words.en: A collegiate system is a system in which a university is divided into colleges, each of which is responsible for the welfare and teaching of its students.

words.tr: phrase. 导师制；辅导制度（一种由导师对学生进行个别或小组指导的教学体系）
words.ex: The university uses a tutorial system for small group teaching.
words.ex_cn: 这所大学使用辅导制度进行小班教学。
words.en: A tutorial system is a method of education in which students are taught in small groups by a tutor, especially in universities in the UK.

words.ex: The corporation sells smartphones worldwide.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司向全球销售智能手机。
words.en: A corporation is a large company or group of companies that is controlled together as a single organization.

words.ex: Going first is a privilege, not a right.
words.ex_cn: 优先权是一种特权，而不是权利。
words.en: A privilege is a special right or advantage that only one person or group has.

words.ex: He is an undergraduate at Harvard.
words.ex_cn: 他是哈佛大学的一名本科生。
words.en: An undergraduate is a student at a university or college who is studying for their first degree.

words.ex: He attended a seminar on climate change.
words.ex_cn: 他参加了一个关于气候变化的研讨会。
words.en: A seminar is a meeting where a group of people discuss a problem or topic.

words.ex: The teacher is very approachable and always smiles.
words.ex_cn: 这位老师非常和蔼可亲，总是面带微笑。
words.en: If you describe someone as approachable, you think that they are friendly and easy to talk to.

words.ex: The bright light stimulated her eyes.
words.ex_cn: 强烈的光线刺激了她的眼睛。
words.en: To stimulate something means to encourage it to begin or develop further.

words.ex: He quit his job because of coercion from his boss.
words.ex_cn: 他因为老板的强迫而辞了工作。
words.en: The act of persuading someone to do something by using force or threats.

words.ex: The team comprises five players and one coach.
words.ex_cn: 这个团队包括五名球员和一名教练。
words.en: If you say that something comprises or is comprised of a number of things or people, you mean it has them as its parts or members.

words.ex: The grandeur of the palace amazed everyone.
words.ex_cn: 宫殿的宏伟让每个人都感到惊讶。
words.en: The quality of being grand or splendid in appearance or style.

words.ex: The archbishop gave a speech at the church.
words.ex_cn: 大主教在教堂发表了一次演讲。
words.en: An archbishop is a bishop of the highest rank who is in charge of an archdiocese.

words.tr:
n. 大学毕业生；
v. 毕业；
words.ex: He is a graduate of Harvard University.
words.ex_cn: 他是哈佛大学的毕业生。
words.en: A graduate is a person who has successfully completed a degree at a university or college and has received a certificate or diploma stating this. To graduate means to successfully complete a degree at a university or college.

words.ex: He is at the forefront of new technology.
words.ex_cn: 他处于新技术的前沿。
words.en: The forefront is the most forward part of something, especially in a literal or metaphorical sense, indicating the leading position in a particular field or activity.

words.ex: He is an influential teacher in our school.
words.ex_cn: 他是我们学校一位有影响力的老师。
words.en: Having great influence on someone or something.

words.tr: adj. 现代的；当代的；同时代的；
words.ex: This museum displays contemporary art.
words.ex_cn: 这个博物馆展示现代艺术。
words.en: Belonging to or occurring in the present; or a person or thing living or existing at the same time as another.

words.tr: n. 威斯康星州（美国中西部的一个州）
words.ex: He lives in Wisconsin.
words.ex_cn: 他住在威斯康星州。
words.en: A state in the northern United States, known for its dairy farming and cheese production.

words.ex: The king proclaimed a new law.
words.ex_cn: 国王宣告了一项新法律。
words.en: If you proclaim something, you formally announce it or declare it publicly.

words.ex: The fence marks the boundary between the two gardens.
words.ex_cn: 这道围栏标志着两个花园的分界线。
words.en: A boundary is a real or imagined line that marks the edge or limit of something.

words.tr:
n. 硬币；金属钱币；
v. 创造；
words.ex: He has a coin in his pocket.
words.ex_cn: 他口袋里有一枚硬币。
words.en: A coin is a small, flat, round piece of metal or plastic that is used as money.

words.tr: adj. 立法的；制定法律的；
words.ex: The legislative branch makes laws.
words.ex_cn: 立法部门制定法律。
words.en: Relating to the making of laws.

words.ex: The beneficent man gave food to the poor.
words.ex_cn: 这位仁慈的人给穷人提供了食物。
words.en: A beneficent person or organization helps people or results in something good.

words.tr:
n. 度假胜地；手段；
v. 求助于；
words.ex: They went to a beach resort for their vacation.
words.ex_cn: 他们去一个海滨度假胜地度假。
words.en: If you resort to a particular course of action, you do it because you cannot see any other way of achieving what you want.

words.tr: adj. 首创性的；先驱性的； v. “pioneer”的现在分词；
words.ex: He made a pioneering discovery in renewable energy.
words.ex_cn: 他在可再生能源领域做出了开创性的发现。
words.en: Involving new ideas or methods, and being the first to use them in a particular field.

words.ex: He takes a correspondence course to learn English at home.
words.ex_cn: 他通过函授课程在家学习英语。
words.en: A course of study in which student and tutors communicate by post.

words.ex: He received compensation for his injured leg.
words.ex_cn: 他因腿部受伤获得了赔偿。
words.en: Compensation is something, typically money, awarded to someone in recognition of loss, suffering, or injury.

words.ex: The faculty of engineering has many labs.
words.ex_cn: 工程学院有许多实验室。
words.en: A faculty is a group of departments in a university or college that specialize in a particular subject or group of subjects, or the teachers in such a group.

words.tr:
n. 律师；劝告
v. 提供咨询；劝告
words.ex: He hired a counsel to defend him in court.
words.ex_cn: 他聘请了一名律师为他在法庭上辩护。
words.en: Counsel refers to the act of giving advice or guidance, especially in a legal context, or to the person who provides such advice.

words.ex: He sat on the chair and read a book.
words.ex_cn: 他坐在椅子上读书。
words.en: A chair is a piece of furniture for one person to sit on, with a back and usually four legs.

words.tr: phrase. 一流的；顶级的；最优的（常用来形容质量或地位最高的事物）
words.ex: He won a blue ribbon at the school fair.
words.ex_cn: 他在学校集市上赢得了一条蓝丝带。
words.en: A blue ribbon is a strip of blue-colored ribbon given as a prize or to indicate high quality or honor.

words.tr:
adj. 牛奶的；乳品的；
n. 乳品店；
words.ex: She bought dairy products from the local farm.
words.ex_cn: 她从当地农场买了乳制品。
words.en: A dairy is a place where milk and cream are kept or where butter and cheese are made.

words.tr:
n. 混凝土；
adj. 具体的；
words.ex: The workers poured concrete to build the foundation.
words.ex_cn: 工人们浇筑混凝土来建造地基。
words.en: Concrete is a hard, strong construction material made by mixing a cementing material (such as Portland cement) and a mineral aggregate (such as sand and gravel) with sufficient water to cause the cement to set and bind the entire mass. In a broader sense, concrete can also refer to something that is tangible, specific, or real.

words.tr: phrase. 甜菜豆：一种旧世界豆科植物属（Melilotus），具有三片复叶叶子，广泛种植用于改良土壤或制作干草...
words.ex: The farmer planted sweet clover to improve the soil quality.
words.ex_cn: 农民种植甜菜豆以改善土壤质量。
words.en: Sweet clover refers to a plant of the genus Melilotus, especially Melilotus officinalis, which is used in agriculture for soil improvement and as a forage crop.

words.ex: He tries to synthesize ideas from different books.
words.ex_cn: 他试图综合来自不同书籍的想法。
words.en: To synthesize means to combine different ideas, influences, or objects into a new whole, or to produce a substance by a chemical reaction in plants or animals.

words.ex: Dicumarol is used as an anticoagulant to prevent blood clotting.
words.ex_cn: 双香豆素用作抗凝剂，以防止血液凝结。
words.en: Dicumarol is a synthetic anticoagulant that acts by inhibiting the synthesis of vitamin K-dependent coagulation factors in the liver.

words.ex: This paper is thinner than that one.
words.ex_cn: 这张纸比那张薄。
words.en: Comparative of thin; having less thickness, width, or density than something else.

words.ex: The wound showed coagulation after a few minutes.
words.ex_cn: 几分钟后，伤口出现了凝固。
words.en: Coagulation is the process by which blood changes from a liquid to a gel, forming a clot.

words.ex: This apple is a variant of the red delicious.
words.ex_cn: 这种苹果是红富士的一个变体。
words.en: A variant is something that is slightly different from other similar things.

words.tr:
n. 凝块；泥团；密集的一群
v. 凝结成块
words.ex: The blood began to clot after the cut.
words.ex_cn: 伤口流血后开始凝固。
words.en: A clot is a sticky lump that forms when blood dries up or becomes thick. If blood clots, it becomes thick and forms a lump.

words.tr: n. 杀鼠灵; [医]华法令阻凝剂
words.ex: The farmer used warfarin to kill rats.
words.ex_cn: 农夫使用杀鼠灵来灭鼠。
words.en: Warfarin is an anticoagulant medication used to prevent blood clots. It works by inhibiting the synthesis of vitamin K-dependent clotting factors.

words.ex: He studies ecology to understand how animals live with plants.
words.ex_cn: 他学习生态学以了解动物如何与植物共存。
words.en: Ecology is the study of the relationships between living organisms, including humans, and their physical environment; it seeks to understand the vital connections between plants and animals and the world around them.

words.ex: She specializes in oncology and treats many cancer patients.
words.ex_cn: 她专攻肿瘤学，治疗了许多癌症患者。
words.en: Oncology is the study and treatment of tumors.

words.tr: n. [病毒] 逆转录酶病毒（一种致肿瘤病毒）
words.ex: Retroviruses are known to cause certain types of cancer.
words.ex_cn: 逆转录病毒被认为会引起某些类型的癌症。
words.en: A retrovirus is a type of virus that inserts a copy of its RNA genome into the DNA of a host cell that it invades, thus changing the genome of that cell.

words.ex: Stem cells have the potential to differentiate into various types of cells.
words.ex_cn: 干细胞有分化成多种类型细胞的潜力。
words.en: A stem cell is a type of cell that has the ability to develop into any type of cell in the body, making them a focus of research in regenerative medicine.

words.tr:
n. 压力；（动植物的）品种；
v. 竭力；
words.ex: The job gave him a lot of strain.
words.ex_cn: 这份工作给他带来了很大的压力。
words.en: To strain means to make a great effort to do something, to pull or stretch something tightly, or to injure a muscle by stretching it too much.

words.ex: The school received accreditation from the government.
words.ex_cn: 这所学校获得了政府的认可。
words.en: Accreditation is the act of granting credit or recognition, especially to an educational institution that maintains suitable standards.

words.ex: Good coordination between teams improves work efficiency.
words.ex_cn: 团队之间的良好协调能提高工作效率。
words.en: The organization of the different elements of a complex body or activity so as to enable them to work together effectively.

words.ex: The church runs an outreach to help homeless people.
words.ex_cn: 这家教堂开展外展服务来帮助无家可归者。
words.en: Outreach refers to the activity of an organization that provides a service or advice to people in the community, especially those who cannot or are unlikely to come to an office, a hospital, etc. for help.

words.ex: Initially, he didn't like the job.
words.ex_cn: 最初，他不喜欢这份工作。
words.en: At the beginning; at first.

words.ex: No example sentences
words.ex_cn: 没有例句
words.en: Prostitution is the practice or occupation of engaging in sexual activity with someone for payment.

words.ex: The traffic on the highway was very heavy this morning.
words.ex_cn: 今天早上高速公路上的交通非常拥堵。
words.en: Traffic refers to the movement of vehicles or people along roads, or to the movement of aircraft, ships, or trains. It can also refer to the trade or exchange of goods or services, especially illegal ones.

words.ex: We will review the meeting agenda tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 我们明天将审查会议议程。
words.en: An agenda is a list or plan of things to be done or considered, especially in a meeting.

words.ex: Exercise helps with your well-being.
words.ex_cn: 锻炼有助于你的健康。
words.en: The state of being comfortable, healthy, or happy.

words.tr: phrase. 家务服务；家庭佣工工作
words.ex: The airline offers a variety of domestic services to major cities.
words.ex_cn: 这家航空公司提供到各大城市的多种国内航线服务。
words.en: Domestic service refers to the work performed in a household, such as cleaning, cooking, and other household chores, typically by a domestic worker.

words.ex: The farmer worked on the plantation every day.
words.ex_cn: 农夫每天在耕地上劳作。
words.en: A plantation is a large piece of land, especially in a tropical country, where crops such as coffee, sugar, rubber, or tobacco are grown.

words.tr: adj. 琐碎的；微不足道的；心胸狭窄的
words.ex: He got angry over a petty mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他因为一个微不足道的错误生气了。
words.en: If you describe someone's behavior as petty, you mean that they care too much about small, unimportant things and perhaps that they are unnecessarily unkind.

words.ex: The exploitation of natural resources helps the economy grow.
words.ex_cn: 自然资源的开发有助于经济发展。
words.en: The action or fact of treating someone unfairly in order to benefit from their work, or the utilization of something for profit or gain.

words.ex: Nigeria is the most populous country in Africa.
words.ex_cn: 尼日利亚是非洲人口最多的国家。
words.en: A country in West Africa, known for its diverse culture, languages, and as the most populous country in Africa.

words.ex: The radio transmits music to listeners.
words.ex_cn: 收音机将音乐传递给听众。
words.en: To send or pass something from one person, place, or thing to another.

words.ex: The teacher gave an assessment of the students' work.
words.ex_cn: 老师对学生的作品进行了评估。
words.en: An assessment is a judgment about something, especially about how good or bad it is, or an amount that is calculated for something, especially for tax purposes.

words.ex: The ever-present threat of terrorism keeps everyone on edge.
words.ex_cn: 经常存在的恐怖主义威胁让每个人都处于紧张状态。
words.en: Always existing or available; constantly encountered.

words.ex: He is learning vocational skills to become a mechanic.
words.ex_cn: 他正在学习职业技能以成为一名机械师。
words.en: Relating to the skills you need to do a particular job.

words.ex: The family had a meagre meal with just bread and water.
words.ex_cn: 这个家庭只吃了一顿贫乏的饭，只有面包和水。
words.en: If you describe an amount or quantity of something as meagre, you are critical of it because it is very small or not enough.

words.ex: Many families live in the slum near the city center.
words.ex_cn: 许多家庭住在城市中心附近的贫民窟里。
words.en: A slum is a heavily populated urban area characterized by substandard housing and squalor.

words.tr: adj. 顺从的；服从的；恭顺的；
words.ex: The submissive dog waited quietly for its owner's command.
words.ex_cn: 这只顺从的狗安静地等待主人的命令。
words.en: If you are submissive, you obey someone without arguing.

words.ex: The new legislation bans plastic bags.
words.ex_cn: 这项新法规禁止使用塑料袋。
words.en: Legislation refers to the process of making or enacting laws by a government or other authority.

words.tr: adj. 司法的；法庭的；审判的；
words.ex: The judicial system protects people's rights.
words.ex_cn: 司法系统保护人民的权利。
words.en: Judicial means relating to the legal system and to judgments made in a court of law.

words.ex: The body has a mechanism to fight viruses.
words.ex_cn: 人体有一种对抗病毒的机制。
words.en: A mechanism is a part of a machine that does a particular task, or a system that is intended to achieve something or deal with a problem.

words.ex: It's a coincidence that we both wore blue today.
words.ex_cn: 我们今天都穿了蓝色，真是巧合。
words.en: A coincidence is when two or more similar or related events occur at the same time by chance and without any planning.

words.tr: n. 津巴布韦（非洲国家）
words.ex: He is from Zimbabwe.
words.ex_cn: 他来自津巴布韦。
words.en: A country in southern Africa, known for its diverse wildlife and landscapes, including the Victoria Falls on the Zambezi River.

words.tr: n. 坦桑尼亚（非洲东部国家）
words.ex: He traveled to Tanzania last summer.
words.ex_cn: 他去年夏天去了坦桑尼亚。
words.en: A country in East Africa known for its vast wilderness areas, including the plains of Serengeti National Park, a safari mecca populated by the 'big five' game (elephant, lion, leopard, buffalo, rhino), and Kilimanjaro National Park, home to Africa's highest mountain.

words.ex: The deterioration of the road made driving dangerous.
words.ex_cn: 道路的恶化使驾驶变得危险。
words.en: The process of becoming progressively worse.

words.ex: The city needs better infrastructure for roads and water.
words.ex_cn: 这座城市需要更好的道路和供水设施。
words.en: The basic physical and organizational structures and facilities (e.g., buildings, roads, power supplies) needed for the operation of a society or enterprise.

words.ex: He became a dropout after failing math class.
words.ex_cn: 他在数学考试不及格后退学了。
words.en: A dropout is a person who leaves school or college before they have finished their studies, especially because they are not interested in continuing.

words.ex: The site of the old church is now a park.
words.ex_cn: 旧教堂的位置现在是一个公园。
words.en: A site is a piece of ground that is used for a particular purpose or where a particular thing happens.

words.ex: The mirror distorts my face.
words.ex_cn: 这面镜子扭曲了我的脸。
words.en: If you distort a statement, fact, or idea, you report or represent it in an untrue way.

words.ex: The government will mobilize troops to help after the earthquake.
words.ex_cn: 政府将调动军队在地震后提供帮助。
words.en: If you mobilize a group of people, or if they mobilize, they prepare to take action, especially in a military context.

words.tr:
n. 接触（的机会或权利）；进入；通道；
v. 获取；使用；接近；
words.ex: Students need access to the library.
words.ex_cn: 学生需要有接触图书馆的机会。
words.en: If you have access to a building or other place, you are able to enter it or use it.

words.ex: The painting is a beautiful representation of nature.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画是对自然的美丽表现。
words.en: A representation of something is a picture, a model of it, or a description of it that you create or that someone else creates for you.

words.ex: The dimension of the box is 10 cm by 5 cm.
words.ex_cn: 这个盒子的尺寸是10厘米乘5厘米。
words.en: A dimension is a measurement of something in a particular direction, or the scope or scale of something.

words.ex: The unemployment rate is an economic indicator.
words.ex_cn: 失业率是一个经济指标。
words.en: An indicator is a measurement or value which gives you an idea of what something is like.

words.ex: The consumption of water has increased this year.
words.ex_cn: 今年水的消耗量增加了。
words.en: Consumption is the act of buying and using products.

words.ex: The system has a vulnerability that hackers can exploit.
words.ex_cn: 这个系统有一个黑客可以利用的脆弱性。
words.en: The state of being exposed to the possibility of being attacked or harmed, either physically or emotionally.

words.tr:
n. 最小值；
adj. 最小量的；
words.ex: The minimum of the function is 5.
words.ex_cn: 这个函数的最小值是5。
words.en: The minimum is the smallest or least amount possible or allowed.

words.tr: adj. 社会的；关于社会的；
words.ex: Social media affects societal behavior.
words.ex_cn: 社交媒体影响社会行为。
words.en: Relating to society or social relations.

words.ex: The norm in this school is to arrive on time.
words.ex_cn: 这所学校的准则就是准时到校。
words.en: A norm is an official standard or level that organizations are expected to reach.

words.tr: adj. 有补助物的，有余格的 v. 补足，补充( complement的过去式和过去分词 )
words.ex: The meal was complemented with a glass of wine.
words.ex_cn: 这顿饭配了一杯葡萄酒。
words.en: To make something complete or perfect by adding something that is missing or needed.

words.ex: The participatory meeting let everyone speak.
words.ex_cn: 这个具有参与特征的会议让每个人都能发言。
words.en: Involving or characterized by participation.

words.ex: The concordance of their opinions surprised everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他们意见的一致性让所有人都感到惊讶。
words.en: A concordance is an alphabetical list of the words in a text or corpus of texts, showing every occurrence of each word with its immediate context. It can also refer to agreement or harmony between people or things.

words.ex: The aggregation of raindrops formed a small puddle.
words.ex_cn: 雨滴的聚集形成了一个小水坑。
words.en: An aggregation is a collection or a group of things or people, often gathered together for a particular purpose.

words.ex: He will assemble the toy for his son.
words.ex_cn: 他将为儿子组装玩具。
words.en: If people assemble or if someone assembles them, they come together in a group, usually for a particular purpose such as a meeting.

words.ex: His conception of the new app was simple but clever.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个新应用的构想简单而巧妙。
words.en: A conception is an idea or a plan that someone has in their mind.

words.ex: The index of 2 in 2^3 is 3.
words.ex_cn: 2^3 中 2 的指数是 3。
words.en: An index is a system by which changes in the value of something and the rate at which it changes can be recorded, measured, or interpreted.

words.ex: He tried to integrate into the new school community.
words.ex_cn: 他试图融入新的学校群体。
words.en: If someone integrates into a social group, or is integrated into it, they behave in such a way that they become part of the group or are accepted into it.

words.tr: v. 举例说明；给书籍、杂志等加插图；
words.ex: The teacher illustrated the point with a simple story.
words.ex_cn: 老师用一个简单的故事来举例说明这个观点。
words.en: To illustrate something means to explain or demonstrate it clearly, often by giving examples or by using pictures or diagrams.

words.ex: His ethnicity is Chinese.
words.ex_cn: 他的种族渊源是中国。
words.en: Ethnicity is the fact or state of belonging to a social group that has a common national or cultural tradition.

words.ex: The fence is a barrier to animals.
words.ex_cn: 这道围栏是动物的障碍。
words.en: A barrier is something such as a rule, law, or policy that makes it difficult or impossible for something to happen or be achieved.

words.tr: adj. 不平坦的；不均匀的；
words.ex: The road is uneven and hard to drive on.
words.ex_cn: 这条路不平坦，很难开车。
words.en: Something that is uneven is not regular, consistent, or equal.

words.ex: The rain persisted all day.
words.ex_cn: 雨持续了一整天。
words.en: If you persist in doing something, you continue to do it even though it is difficult or other people are against it.

words.ex: The millennium began in the year 2000.
words.ex_cn: 一千年始于2000年。
words.en: A millennium is a period of one thousand years.

words.ex: The test has only numerical answers.
words.ex_cn: 这个测试只有数字答案。
words.en: Numerical means relating to numbers or consisting of numbers.

words.tr: adj. 可以计量的；可量化的
words.ex: The results are quantifiable and clear.
words.ex_cn: 这些结果是可以量化的，而且清晰。
words.en: If something is quantifiable, it can be measured or expressed in numbers.

words.ex: He can identify the bird by its song.
words.ex_cn: 他能通过鸟的叫声识别它。
words.en: If you can identify someone or something, you are able to recognize them or distinguish them from others.

words.ex: The mortality rate in the region increased last year.
words.ex_cn: 去年该地区的死亡率上升了。
words.en: Mortality refers to the state of being subject to death or the number of deaths in a particular population or period.

words.tr: adj. 母亲的；母性的；母系的；
words.ex: Her maternal love kept the family strong.
words.ex_cn: 她的母爱让家庭保持坚强。
words.en: Maternal feelings or actions are typical of a kind, loving mother.

words.ex: He got malaria from a mosquito bite.
words.ex_cn: 他被蚊子叮咬后得了疟疾。
words.en: Malaria is a disease caused by a parasite that is transmitted to humans through the bites of infected mosquitoes.

words.ex: The city plans for sustainability by using solar energy.
words.ex_cn: 这座城市通过使用太阳能来实现可持续性。
words.en: Sustainability is the ability to maintain or support a process continuously over time. In the context of environmental science, it refers to the avoidance of the depletion of natural resources in order to maintain an ecological balance.

words.ex: He has the capacity to solve hard math problems.
words.ex_cn: 他有能力解决复杂的数学问题。
words.en: The capacity of a place or container is the amount of things or people that it can hold.

words.ex: Good governance helps the city run smoothly.
words.ex_cn: 良好的治理有助于城市顺利运行。
words.en: The way that a country, company, etc. is controlled by the people who run it.

words.tr: n. 索福克勒斯（古希腊悲剧诗人）
words.ex: Sophocles is one of the three great ancient Greek tragedians.
words.ex_cn: 索福克勒斯是古希腊三大悲剧诗人之一。
words.en: Sophocles was one of the three ancient Greek tragedians whose plays have survived. His first plays were written later than those of Aeschylus, and earlier than or contemporary with those of Euripides. Sophocles wrote over 120 plays during the course of his life, but only seven have survived in a complete form.

words.tr:
n. 雅典人
adj. 雅典的
words.ex: The Athenian philosopher Socrates is one of the most famous thinkers in history.
words.ex_cn: 雅典哲学家苏格拉底是历史上最著名的思想家之一。
words.en: Of or relating to Athens, its people, or its culture.

words.ex: He is a famous playwright who writes plays.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位著名的剧作家，写剧本。
words.en: A playwright is a person who writes plays.

words.tr: n. 埃斯库罗斯（古希腊悲剧诗人）
words.ex: Aeschylus is considered one of the greatest tragedians of ancient Greece.
words.ex_cn: 埃斯库罗斯被认为是古希腊最伟大的悲剧作家之一。
words.en: Aeschylus was an ancient Greek tragedian, often described as the father of tragedy. He is the first of the three Greek tragedians whose plays have survived, the others being Sophocles and Euripides.

words.ex: The book encompasses all basic math skills.
words.ex_cn: 这本书包含了所有基础数学技能。
words.en: If something encompasses particular things, it includes them.

words.tr: n. （Oedipus）俄狄浦斯（希腊神话人物）; adj. （Oedipus）恋母情结的
words.ex: Oedipus was a tragic figure in Greek mythology.
words.ex_cn: 俄狄浦斯是希腊神话中的悲剧人物。
words.en: In Greek mythology, Oedipus was the king of Thebes who unwittingly killed his father and married his mother.

words.ex: The ancient people worshipped a sun deity.
words.ex_cn: 古人崇拜太阳神。
words.en: A deity is a god or goddess, or anything revered as divine.

words.tr: n. （Dionysus）迪奥尼索司（希腊神话中的酒神）; n. （Dionysus）（美）迭昂丽稣...
words.ex: Dionysus, the god of wine and revelry, was often depicted with a crown of vine leaves.
words.ex_cn: 酒神迪奥尼索司，常被描绘为戴着葡萄藤叶冠的形象。
words.en: In Greek mythology, Dionysus is the god of wine, fertility, and ritual ecstasy.

words.tr: n. 优势；有利条件；好处；
words.ex: His height gives him an advantage in basketball.
words.ex_cn: 他的身高在篮球中给了他优势。
words.en: An advantage is a factor or circumstance that puts you in a favorable or superior position.

words.ex: The hapless boy lost his wallet and got caught in the rain.
words.ex_cn: 这个倒霉的男孩丢了钱包，还被雨淋了。
words.en: If you describe someone as hapless, you mean that they are unlucky or unfortunate.

words.tr: n. 底比斯（古埃及城市）
words.ex: Thebes was once the capital of ancient Egypt.
words.ex_cn: 底比斯曾是古埃及的首都。
words.en: Thebes is the Greek name for a city in Ancient Egypt, known for its temples and as a political and religious center.

words.tr: n. 拉伊俄斯（希腊神话中的人物，俄狄浦斯的父亲）
words.ex: In Greek mythology, Laius was the king of Thebes and the father of Oedipus.
words.ex_cn: 在希腊神话中，拉伊俄斯是底比斯的国王，也是俄狄浦斯的父亲。
words.en: A type of traditional Chinese poetry with a specific structure, often characterized by its lyrical and reflective nature.

words.tr: n. 伊俄卡斯忒（希腊神话中俄狄浦斯的母亲和妻子）
words.ex: In the play, Jocasta is torn between her love for her son and the horror of their incestuous relationship.
words.ex_cn: 在戏剧中，伊俄卡斯忒在对她儿子的爱和对他们乱伦关系的恐惧之间挣扎。
words.en: In Greek mythology, the wife of Laius and mother of Oedipus, whom she unwittingly married.

words.ex: The priest was known as an oracle who spoke for the gods.
words.ex_cn: 这位祭司被称为传达神谕的传神谕者。
words.en: An oracle is a person or thing considered to provide wise and insightful guidance or prophetic predictions, often through divine inspiration.

words.tr: n. 阿波罗（希腊神话中的太阳神）
words.ex: Apollo is often depicted with a radiant crown and holding a lyre.
words.ex_cn: 阿波罗常被描绘成戴着光芒四射的冠冕，手持里拉琴。
words.en: In Greek mythology, Apollo is the god of the sun, music, and poetry. The Apollo program was a series of space missions undertaken by the United States with the goal of landing a man on the Moon and returning him safely to Earth.

words.ex: Delphi is famous for its ancient oracle.
words.ex_cn: 特尔斐以其古老的预言家而闻名。
words.en: Delphi: An ancient Greek city, known for the oracle of Apollo.

words.tr: n. 异兆；凶兆；不祥之兆
words.ex: The dark clouds were a portent of the coming storm.
words.ex_cn: 乌云是即将到来的风暴的前兆。
words.en: A portent is an event or sign that is considered to indicate what is going to happen in the future, especially something very good or very bad.

words.ex: The ruins show the antiquity of this civilization.
words.ex_cn: 这些废墟展示了这个文明的古老。
words.en: The ancient past, especially the period before the Middle Ages.

words.ex: There was a spike in sales after the advertisement.
words.ex_cn: 广告发布后，销量出现了激增。
words.en: A spike is a thin, pointed piece of metal, wood, or another hard material, or a sudden increase in something.

words.tr:
v. 向旁侧避让；回避
n. 向侧方跨步
words.ex: He sidestepped the question during the interview.
words.ex_cn: 他在采访中回避了这个问题。
words.en: If you sidestep a problem or question, you avoid answering it or dealing with it.

words.ex: The farmer piled up fodder for the cows.
words.ex_cn: 农夫为奶牛堆了一堆饲料。
words.en: Fodder is food that is given to cows, horses, and other animals.

words.tr: n. 科林斯（希腊南部城市）
words.ex: The ancient city of Corinth was a significant hub during the Roman Empire.
words.ex_cn: 古科林斯城在罗马帝国时期是一个重要的枢纽。
words.en: Corinth is an ancient city in Greece, known for its historical significance and archaeological sites.

words.tr: n. 波吕玻斯（古希腊神话中的人物，俄狄浦斯王的养父）
words.ex: Polybus was the foster father of Oedipus in Greek mythology.
words.ex_cn: 在希腊神话中，波吕玻斯是俄狄浦斯王的养父。
words.en: In Greek mythology, the king of Corinth who raised Oedipus as his own son.

words.tr: n. 墨洛珀（希腊神话中七仙女之一）
words.ex: Merope was one of the Pleiades, the seven daughters of Atlas and Pleione in Greek mythology.
words.ex_cn: 墨洛珀是七仙女之一，是希腊神话中阿特拉斯和普勒俄涅的七个女儿之一。
words.en: In Greek mythology, the wife of Sisyphus and mother of Odysseus.

words.ex: The movie showed a gruesome accident.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影展示了一起令人毛骨悚然的事故。
words.en: Something that is gruesome is extremely unpleasant and shocking, especially because it involves death or injury.

words.ex: The jury gave a guilty verdict.
words.ex_cn: 陪审团作出了有罪裁决。
words.en: A verdict is a decision made after a lot of consideration, especially one made by a jury in a court of law.

words.tr: n. 揭露；被揭示的真相；
words.ex: The letter was a revelation about his secret life.
words.ex_cn: 这封信揭露了他隐秘的生活。
words.en: A revelation is a surprising and previously unknown fact that has been disclosed to others.

words.ex: The two roads converge at the town center.
words.ex_cn: 这两条路在镇中心交汇。
words.en: If roads or lines converge, they meet or join at a particular place.

words.tr: adj. 原始的；远古的；最初的
words.ex: The primordial soup formed the first life on Earth.
words.ex_cn: 原始汤形成了地球上的最初生命。
words.en: Primordial means existing at or from the beginning of time; primeval.

words.tr: n. 老人，乡下老头，领班
words.ex: The gaffer on the film set was responsible for organizing the crew.
words.ex_cn: 电影拍摄现场的领班负责组织工作人员。
words.en: 1. A gaffer is the person in charge of the workers on a film set or in a factory. 2. An old man, especially one who is in charge of a group of people.

words.ex: The castle endured a long siege during the war.
words.ex_cn: 这座城堡在战争中经历了长期的围攻。
words.en: A siege is a military operation in which enemy forces surround a town or building, cutting off essential supplies, with the aim of compelling those inside to surrender.

words.ex: The accident looked horrendous.
words.ex_cn: 那场事故看起来很可怕。
words.en: If you describe something as horrendous, you are emphasizing that it is very unpleasant or shocking.

words.tr: n. （古埃及）狮身人面像；难于理解的人；天蛾
words.ex: The sphinx sits near the pyramids in Egypt.
words.ex_cn: 狮身人面像坐落在埃及的金字塔附近。
words.en: A sphinx is a mythical creature with the body of a lion and the head of a human, often depicted as a guardian figure.

words.tr: phrase. 切断；中止；扼杀（供应、流动或进程等）
words.ex: The police tried to choke off the supply of illegal drugs.
words.ex_cn: 警方试图切断非法毒品的供应。
words.en: To stop or prevent something from continuing or developing.

words.tr: adj. 绝望的；孤立无助的；被弃置的
words.ex: The forlorn dog sat by the door, waiting for its owner.
words.ex_cn: 那条孤单的狗坐在门边，等待它的主人。
words.en: If someone is forlorn, they feel alone and unhappy.

words.ex: The herald announced the king's arrival.
words.ex_cn: 传令官宣布了国王的到来。
words.en: A herald is someone who carries or proclaims important news; a forerunner or harbinger.

words.ex: The problem was solved ingeniously.
words.ex_cn: 这个问题被巧妙地解决了。
words.en: In a manner showing cleverness or originality in solving problems or in inventing.

words.ex: There was a scramble for the last ticket.
words.ex_cn: 大家争相抢购最后一张票。
words.en: If you scramble over rocks or up a hill, you move quickly over them or up it using your hands to help you. Scramble can also mean to compete or struggle with others for something that is in short supply.

words.tr: n. 基塞龙山（希腊中部山脉）
words.ex: The ancient Athenians believed that the mountain Cithaeron was sacred.
words.ex_cn: 古雅典人认为基塞龙山是神圣的。
words.en: A mountain in Boeotia, Greece, associated with the myth of Oedipus.

words.tr: phrase. 把某人冒充成…；把某人伪装成…
words.ex: He tried to pass himself off as a famous actor.
words.ex_cn: 他试图把自己冒充成一个著名演员。
words.en: To present someone as something they are not, especially in order to deceive others.

words.ex: The army besiege the small town.
words.ex_cn: 军队围攻这座小镇。
words.en: To surround a place with armed forces in order to capture it or force its surrender; to overwhelm someone with requests or complaints.

words.tr: n. 克瑞翁（希腊神话中的人物，特洛伊战争中的英雄）
words.ex: Creon was a prominent figure in Greek mythology.
words.ex_cn: 克瑞翁是希腊神话中的一个重要人物。
words.en: In Greek mythology, the brother of Jocasta and uncle of Oedipus, who becomes king of Thebes.

words.ex: The priest offered prayers for the expiation of sins.
words.ex_cn: 牧师为赎罪祈祷。
words.en: The act of making amends or reparation for guilt or wrongdoing; atonement.

words.ex: The police caught the culprit who stole the bike.
words.ex_cn: 警察抓住了偷自行车的罪犯。
words.en: A culprit is someone who has done something wrong or illegal.

words.ex: He took a circuitous route to avoid the traffic.
words.ex_cn: 他绕了远路以避开交通拥堵。
words.en: A circuitous route, journey, or piece of writing is longer than it needs to be because it is not direct.

words.tr: n. 泰瑞西阿斯（希腊神话中的盲人先知）
words.ex: Teiresias tells the truth to Oedipus.
words.ex_cn: 提瑞西阿斯向俄狄浦斯说出真相。
words.en: In Greek mythology, Teiresias was a blind prophet of Thebes, famous for clairvoyance and for being transformed into a woman for seven years.

words.ex: The linchpin holds the wheel in place.
words.ex_cn: 制轮楔将车轮固定到位。
words.en: A linchpin is a person or thing that is essential to the success or operation of something.

words.tr:
n. 突然倾斜；急动；踉跄
v. 突然倾斜；急动；踉跄
words.ex: The boat made a sudden lurch to the left.
words.ex_cn: 船突然向左倾斜。
words.en: If you lurch, you move suddenly and uncontrollably in one direction.

words.ex: The flame singed her hair.
words.ex_cn: 火焰烧焦了她的头发。
words.en: To burn superficially or lightly; scorch.

words.tr: phrase. v. 观察某人；查看某人的情况；对某人进行打量或评估
words.ex: I will check you out at the front desk.
words.ex_cn: 我会在前台为你办理退房。
words.en: To investigate or examine someone, typically to find out more about them or to ensure they are not carrying anything illegal.

words.ex: They conspire to cheat on the test.
words.ex_cn: 他们密谋在考试中作弊。
words.en: If two or more people or groups conspire to do something illegal or harmful, they make a secret agreement to do it.

words.tr: n. 计划者，阴谋家，谋士
words.ex: He is a schemer who plans to cheat others.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个计划欺骗他人的阴谋家。
words.en: A schemer is someone who makes secret and often dishonest plans to get what they want.

words.tr:
adj. 恼火的；激怒的
v. 使恼怒；使恶化；使加剧；“exasperate”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: He was exasperated by the loud noise.
words.ex_cn: 他被那阵噪音气得发疯。
words.en: If you describe someone as exasperated, you mean that they are frustrated or angry because of something that is happening or something that another person is doing.

words.tr:
n. 争吵
v. 争吵
words.ex: The two boys squabble over toys every day.
words.ex_cn: 这两个男孩每天为玩具争吵。
words.en: A squabble is a noisy disagreement about something unimportant.

words.ex: The village was destroyed by pestilence last year.
words.ex_cn: 去年这个村庄被瘟疫摧毁了。
words.en: A pestilence is a fatal epidemic disease, especially bubonic plague.

words.tr:
n. 情节；小块用地；
v. 绘图；
words.ex: The plot of the movie was very exciting.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影的情节非常精彩。
words.en: A plot is a secret plan by a group of people to do something that is illegal or wrong, especially against a person or a government. It can also refer to the main events of a play, novel, movie, or similar work, devised and presented by the writer as an interrelated sequence. Additionally, a plot can be a small piece of land that is used or intended for a specific purpose.

words.tr:
n. 妥协；
v. 危及；
words.ex: They reached a compromise after hours of talk.
words.ex_cn: 经过数小时的讨论，他们达成了妥协。
words.en: A compromise is an agreement between two people or groups in which each side gives up some of the things they want so that both sides are happy at the end.

words.ex: Helios drives his sun chariot across the sky.
words.ex_cn: 赫利俄斯驾驶他的太阳战车划过天空。
words.en: In Greek mythology, Helios is the god of the sun, often depicted as driving a chariot across the sky from east to west each day.

words.tr: adv. 成碎片地；弄碎地；分离地
words.ex: The kingdom was torn asunder by civil war.
words.ex_cn: 这个王国因内战而被撕裂。
words.en: Into parts or pieces; apart.

words.tr:
n. 耻辱；丢脸；不光彩
v. 使丢脸；使蒙受耻辱
words.ex: He felt disgrace after lying to his friends.
words.ex_cn: 他向朋友撒谎后感到羞愧。
words.en: If you say that someone is in disgrace, you are emphasizing that other people disapprove of them and do not respect them because of something that they have done.

words.ex: The old seer predicted rain tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 那位老先知预言明天会下雨。
words.en: A seer is someone who is believed to be able, through supernatural insight, to see what the future holds.

words.tr: n. 福基斯（希腊中部古地区）
words.ex: Phocis is an ancient region in Greece.
words.ex_cn: 福基斯是希腊的一个古代地区。
words.en: A region in central Greece, home to the Oracle of Delphi.

words.ex: He dawdled away the afternoon at the park.
words.ex_cn: 他在公园里混掉了整个下午。
words.en: If you dawdle, you spend more time than is necessary going somewhere or doing something.

words.ex: The weather was dire, with heavy rain and strong winds.
words.ex_cn: 天气非常可怕，下着大雨，刮着大风。
words.en: If you describe a situation as dire, you are emphasizing that it is very bad or serious.

words.tr: n. 放牧；草场； v. 吃草；“graze”的现在分词；
words.ex: The farmers practice grazing on the open land.
words.ex_cn: 农民们在开阔的土地上进行放牧。
words.en: The act of animals feeding on grass or the land where such feeding occurs.

chapters.name: Unit 10 Reflections on Wars Text A

words.ex: The clarity of her explanation helped everyone understand.
words.ex_cn: 她解释的清晰帮助了每个人理解。
words.en: Clarity is the quality of being clear, in particular the quality of being easy to understand or see.

words.ex: He gave a precise answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了准确的答案。
words.en: If you give precise information or precise instructions, you give exact details so that there is no confusion about what should be done.

words.ex: The river forms the border between the two countries.
words.ex_cn: 这条河是两个国家的边界。
words.en: The edge or boundary of something, or the part near it; a dividing line.

words.tr: adj. 合法的；法律认可的；合理的；
words.ex: This contract is legitimate and signed by both parties.
words.ex_cn: 这份合同是合法的，并由双方签署。
words.en: Something that is legitimate is acceptable according to the law.

words.ex: A car has many components, like wheels and engines.
words.ex_cn: 汽车有许多部分，比如轮子和发动机。
words.en: A component is a part of a larger whole, especially a part that can be separated from or attached to a system.

words.tr:
n. 代表；典型事物；
adj. 典型的；有代表性的；代议制的；
words.ex: He is the representative of our class.
words.ex_cn: 他是我们班的代表。
words.en: A representative is a person who has been chosen to act or make decisions on behalf of another person or a group of people.

words.tr: phrase. 萨达姆·侯赛因（伊拉克前总统，1979–2003 年在位）
words.ex: Saddam Hussein was the president of Iraq.
words.ex_cn: 萨达姆·侯赛因是伊拉克的总统。
words.en: The former President of Iraq (1979–2003), known for his authoritarian rule and the Gulf War.

words.ex: He tried to conceal the truth.
words.ex_cn: 他试图隐藏真相。
words.en: If you conceal something, you prevent it from being seen or known about.

words.ex: The team was unanimous in choosing the new leader.
words.ex_cn: 团队在选择新领导时意见完全一致。
words.en: When a group of people are unanimous, they all agree about something or all vote for the same thing.

words.ex: France was an ally of the United States in the war.
words.ex_cn: 法国在战争中是美国的同盟者。
words.en: An ally is a country, organization, or person that helps and supports another country, organization, or person in a difficult situation.

words.tr: phrase. 沙特阿拉伯（国家名）
words.ex: He lives in Saudi Arabia.
words.ex_cn: 他住在沙特阿拉伯。
words.en: Saudi Arabia is a country in the Middle East, known for its Islamic culture, vast deserts, and being the birthplace of Islam. It is also the world's largest oil exporter.

words.tr: adj. 正在进行中的；航行中的；
words.ex: The project is underway.
words.ex_cn: 这个项目正在进行中。
words.en: If something is underway, it is happening now.

words.ex: He lives in Baghdad.
words.ex_cn: 他住在巴格达。
words.en: The capital city of Iraq, located in the central part of the country along the Tigris River.

words.ex: He receives his wage every Friday.
words.ex_cn: 他每周五领工资。
words.en: A wage is the money that someone is paid each week by their employer, especially for manual or unskilled work. To wage means to carry on (a war or campaign).

words.ex: My mentor helped me choose my career path.
words.ex_cn: 我的导师帮助我选择了职业道路。
words.en: A mentor is a person who gives a younger or less experienced person help and advice over a period of time, especially at work or school.

words.tr:
v. 禁止；
n. 禁止；
words.ex: The school bans phones in class.
words.ex_cn: 学校禁止在课堂上使用手机。
words.en: If there is a ban on something, it is not allowed. If something is banned, it is not allowed to be done, shown, or used.

words.ex: The meaning of the poem is obscure.
words.ex_cn: 这首诗的意思不清楚。
words.en: If something is obscure, it is not well known or not easily understood.

words.tr: n. 自明之理；不言而喻的道理；老生常谈
words.ex: It is a truism that water boils at 100 degrees Celsius.
words.ex_cn: 水在100摄氏度沸腾，这是一个不言而喻的事实。
words.en: A truism is a statement that is obviously true and says nothing new or interesting.

words.ex: The adherence of the sticker to the wall is strong.
words.ex_cn: 贴纸对墙的粘附很强。
words.en: Adherence is the act of following or sticking to a particular set of beliefs, principles, or rules.

words.ex: We must eliminate the waste to protect the environment.
words.ex_cn: 我们必须消除浪费以保护环境。
words.en: To eliminate something, especially something you do not want or need, means to remove it completely.

words.tr: adj. 心照不宣的；不作声的
words.ex: They have a tacit understanding about the rules.
words.ex_cn: 他们对规则有一种心照不宣的理解。
words.en: If you refer to someone's tacit agreement or approval, you mean they are agreeing to something or approving it without actually saying so, often because they are unwilling to admit to doing so.

words.tr: v. 扫；“sweep”的现在分词； adj. 全面的；
words.ex: He sweeping the floor every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上扫地。
words.en: If you describe something as sweeping, you mean it is very extensive or has a very wide effect.

words.tr: adj. 适当的；合适的；恰当的；
words.ex: This dress is appropriate for a wedding.
words.ex_cn: 这条裙子适合参加婚礼。
words.en: Something that is appropriate is suitable or acceptable for a particular situation.

words.ex: He has ideological beliefs about freedom.
words.ex_cn: 他有关于自由的思想信念。
words.en: Relating to or concerned with ideas, especially of a political or economic nature.

words.ex: The bully tried to intimidate the new student.
words.ex_cn: 那个霸凌者试图恐吓新生。
words.en: If you intimidate someone, you deliberately make them frightened enough to do what you want them to do.

words.tr: v. 逐步渗透；逐渐灌输
words.ex: Parents try to instill good habits in their children.
words.ex_cn: 父母试图在孩子身上培养良好的习惯。
words.en: To instill something in someone means to gradually but firmly establish an idea or attitude in their mind.

words.ex: The storm disrupted the train service.
words.ex_cn: 这场风暴中断了火车服务。
words.en: To disrupt a system, process, or event means to prevent it from continuing or operating in a normal way.

words.ex: He spoke constructively during the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他在会议上积极地发言。
words.en: In a way that is intended to help or improve something.

words.tr: 专有名词，指奥萨马·本·拉登（Osama bin Laden），基地组织领导人
words.ex: No example sentences
words.ex_cn: 没有例句
words.en: The founder of the militant group al-Qaeda, responsible for the September 11 attacks.

words.ex: Water is indispensable for life.
words.ex_cn: 水对生命是必不可少的。
words.en: Absolutely necessary or essential.

chapters.name: Unit 10 Reflections on Wars Text B

words.tr: n. 奥许维次（波兰城市名）; n. （Auschwitz）人名；（德）奥施维茨
words.ex: He visited Auschwitz to learn about history.
words.ex_cn: 他参观了奥斯维辛以了解历史。
words.en: A network of Nazi German concentration and extermination camps in occupied Poland during World War II.

words.tr: n. 比克瑙（波兰地名，曾是纳粹集中营所在地）
words.ex: He visited Birkenau to learn about history.
words.ex_cn: 他去比克瑙参观以了解历史。
words.en: A subcamp of Auschwitz, also a major extermination camp during the Holocaust.

words.ex: The food supply was inadequate for the number of people.
words.ex_cn: 食物供应对人数来说是不充分的。
words.en: If something is inadequate, there is not enough of it or it is not good enough.

words.ex: He must confront his fears.
words.ex_cn: 他必须面对自己的恐惧。
words.en: If you confront a difficult situation or issue, you accept the fact that it exists and try to deal with it.

words.ex: It is rational to save money for the future.
words.ex_cn: 为未来存钱是合理的。
words.en: Based on or in accordance with reason or logic.

words.ex: His testimony proved the suspect was innocent.
words.ex_cn: 他的证词证明了嫌疑人是无辜的。
words.en: A formal written or spoken statement, especially one given in a court of law.

words.ex: He is a descendant of the first king.
words.ex_cn: 他是第一位国王的后裔。
words.en: A person, plant, or animal that is descended from a particular ancestor.

words.ex: The farmer tried to exterminate the rats.
words.ex_cn: 农夫试图消灭老鼠。
words.en: To exterminate means to kill all the members of a group of people or animals, or to destroy something completely.

words.ex: The manifestation of his anger was a loud shout.
words.ex_cn: 他愤怒的显示是一声大喊。
words.en: A manifestation is an event, action, or object that clearly shows or embodies something, especially a theory or an abstract idea.

words.tr:
n. 纳粹党人
adj. 纳粹党的
words.ex: He hated the nazi regime.
words.ex_cn: 他憎恨纳粹政权。
words.en: A member of the National Socialist German Workers' Party, which controlled Germany from 1933 to 1945 under Adolf Hitler.

words.tr: adj. 恶魔（般）的；邪恶的；超乎常人的
words.ex: The demon had a demonic laugh.
words.ex_cn: 那个恶魔有一种邪恶的笑声。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as demonic, you mean that they are fierce, evil, or frightening.

words.ex: The bicycle was a precursor to the car.
words.ex_cn: 自行车是汽车的先驱。
words.en: A precursor is something that happened or existed before another thing, especially if it either developed into it or had an influence on it.

words.ex: The medicine helps reduce inhibition of the immune system.
words.ex_cn: 这种药物有助于抑制免疫系统的抑制。
words.en: Inhibition is a feeling that makes one self-conscious and unable to act in a relaxed and natural way.

words.ex: He votes in a democratic election.
words.ex_cn: 他在民主选举中投票。
words.en: A democratic country, government, or political system is governed by representatives who are elected by the people.

words.tr: v. 奴役；征服；使受控制
words.ex: The cruel king tried to enslave the villagers.
words.ex_cn: 这个残酷的国王试图奴役村民。
words.en: To make someone a slave; to take away someone's freedom.

words.ex: He screamed in agony after the fall.
words.ex_cn: 他摔倒后痛苦地大叫。
words.en: Agony is very severe physical or mental pain.

words.ex: This tradition originates from ancient times.
words.ex_cn: 这个传统起源于古代。
words.en: To originate means to have a specific beginning or to start something.

words.ex: He called for help in desperation.
words.ex_cn: 他绝望地呼救。
words.en: Desperation is the feeling that you have when you are in such a bad situation that you are willing to take any risk to change it.

words.tr:
n. 极端主义者；过激分子
adj. 极端主义的；过激的
words.ex: The extremist refused to listen to others.
words.ex_cn: 这个极端分子拒绝倾听别人的意见。
words.en: An extremist is someone who has extreme political or religious ideas and is willing to do things that are illegal, violent, or not normal in order to achieve their aims.

words.ex: The enforcement of traffic laws keeps roads safe.
words.ex_cn: 交通法规的执行使道路更安全。
words.en: The act of compelling observance of or compliance with a law, rule, or obligation.

words.tr: n. 新纳粹分子；新纳粹主义者
words.ex: No example sentences
words.ex_cn: 没有例句
words.en: A neo-Nazi is someone who supports or belongs to a modern political organization that has beliefs similar to those of the Nazis.

words.ex: His speech was called incitement to violence.
words.ex_cn: 他的演讲被称为煽动暴力。
words.en: The act of encouraging someone to do something violent, illegal, or unpleasant, especially by making them angry or excited.

words.ex: The Holocaust killed millions of Jews during World War II.
words.ex_cn: 大屠杀在二战期间杀害了数百万犹太人。
words.en: The Holocaust refers to the genocide of European Jews and others by the Nazis during World War II.

words.ex: The invention of the internet changed our era.
words.ex_cn: 互联网的发明改变了我们的时代。
words.en: An era is a period of time that is considered as a single unit because of a particular characteristic or event.

words.ex: He kept his dignity even when he was poor.
words.ex_cn: 即使他很穷，他依然保持尊严。
words.en: Dignity is the quality of being worthy of honor or respect.

words.ex: They tried to desecrate the holy church.
words.ex_cn: 他们试图亵渎那座神圣的教堂。
words.en: To desecrate something means to spoil or damage something that is considered to be holy or very important.

words.ex: The shoah was a terrible time in history.
words.ex_cn: 大屠杀是历史上一段可怕的时期。
words.en: The term 'Shoah' refers specifically to the Holocaust, the genocide of six million Jews by the Nazi regime and its collaborators during World War II.

words.ex: It is a convention to shake hands when you meet someone.
words.ex_cn: 见面时握手是一种习俗。
words.en: A convention is a large meeting of an organization or political group, or a way of behaving that is considered to be correct or polite by most people in a society.

words.ex: The war led to the genocide of many innocent people.
words.ex_cn: 这场战争导致了众多无辜人民的种族灭绝。
words.en: Genocide is the deliberate killing of a large number of people from a particular nation or ethnic group with the aim of destroying that nation or group.

words.tr:
n. 开始；启动；创业
adj. 启动阶段的；创业所需的
words.ex: The start-up of the new factory took two months.
words.ex_cn: 新工厂的启动花了两个月。
words.en: A start-up is a new business venture, typically in the technology sector, that is in the initial stages of operation, often characterized by high uncertainty and risk but also by the potential for rapid growth and scalability.

words.tr: adj. 士兵的；一般大众的
words.ex: The union represents the interests of the rank-and-file members.
words.ex_cn: 工会代表了一般成员的利益。
words.en: The ordinary members of an organization or group, as opposed to its leaders or officers.

words.ex: There was a scramble for the last ticket.
words.ex_cn: 大家争相抢购最后一张票。
words.en: If you scramble over rocks or up a hill, you move quickly over them or up it using your hands to help you. Scramble can also mean to compete or struggle with others for something that is in short supply.

words.tr:
v. 发射；发起；启动；
n. 发射；投掷；启动；
words.ex: They will launch a rocket tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他们明天将发射一枚火箭。
words.en: To launch something means to send it into the air, space, or water, especially with a lot of force or effort, or to start an activity, event, or project.

words.ex: He is well-versed in the lore of ancient civilizations.
words.ex_cn: 他对古代文明的知识了如指掌。
words.en: Knowledge and traditions relating to a particular subject or held by a particular group.

words.ex: The children line up to enter the classroom.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们排队进入教室。
words.en: To arrange people or things in a row or to arrange for an event or activity to happen.

words.tr:
n. 冒险事业；商业冒险；投机；
v. 冒险；投机；
words.ex: He started a new venture in technology.
words.ex_cn: 他创办了一项新的科技冒险事业。
words.en: If you venture somewhere, you go somewhere that might be dangerous. If you venture a question or statement, you say it in an uncertain way because you are afraid it might be stupid or wrong.

words.tr: phrase. 十拿九稳的事；可靠的选择
words.ex: It is a safe bet that he will pass the test.
words.ex_cn: 他通过考试是稳操胜券的。
words.en: A reliable or certain choice or prediction.

words.ex: He will install the new software on his computer.
words.ex_cn: 他将在他的电脑上安装新软件。
words.en: To set up or fix in position for use or service.

words.ex: He used the sun to orient himself.
words.ex_cn: 他用太阳来确定方向。
words.en: To orient means to align or position something in relation to the points of a compass or other specified positions, or to familiarize someone with a new situation or environment.

words.tr: adj. 不成则败的；孤注一掷的
words.ex: This exam is make-or-break for her future.
words.ex_cn: 这次考试对她的未来至关重要。
words.en: A make-or-break situation is one that will bring great success or complete failure.

words.ex: He went on a shopping spree last weekend.
words.ex_cn: 他上周末进行了一次疯狂购物。
words.en: A spree is a short period of time during which you do a lot of something, often something that you do not normally do and that you enjoy.

words.ex: The company plans to recruit new staff next month.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司计划下个月招聘新员工。
words.en: To recruit means to enlist someone in the armed forces or to persuade someone to join a company, organization, or group.

words.ex: He is a strong contender for the championship.
words.ex_cn: 他是冠军的有力竞争者。
words.en: A contender is someone who takes part in a competition or tries to win something.

words.ex: The school will rescind the rule next month.
words.ex_cn: 学校下个月将撤销这项规定。
words.en: If a government or a group of people in power rescind a law or agreement, they officially withdraw it and state that it is no longer valid.

words.tr: adj. 有法律约束力的；必须遵守的； n. 封皮； v. “bind”的现在分词；
words.ex: The contract is binding for both parties.
words.ex_cn: 这份合同对双方都有法律约束力。
words.en: Binding refers to the act of fastening or securing something, or the material used to do this. It can also describe something that is obligatory or that imposes a legal or moral obligation.

words.ex: The gross income of the company is $5 million.
words.ex_cn: 公司的总收入是500万美元。
words.en: If you describe something as gross, you mean it is very obvious, unacceptable, or unpleasant.

words.tr: v. 解释说明；“account”的现在分词； n. 会计；会计学；
words.ex: He is accounting for his absence.
words.ex_cn: 他正在解释他的缺席。
words.en: Accounting is the process of keeping financial accounts.

words.ex: The politician used manipulation to win the election.
words.ex_cn: 这位政治家通过操纵赢得了选举。
words.en: Manipulation refers to the act of controlling or influencing someone or something in a skillful but often unfair or dishonest way.

words.tr:
adv. 彻底地；立刻地；
adj. 完全的；彻底的；
words.ex: He refused the offer outright.
words.ex_cn: 他彻底拒绝了这个提议。
words.en: If something is done outright, it is done completely and without any hesitation or attempt to hide it.

words.ex: The man was punished for fraud.
words.ex_cn: 这个人因欺骗而受到惩罚。
words.en: Fraud is the crime of gaining money or financial benefits by a trick or by lying.

words.ex: He faced a dilemma: stay home or go to work.
words.ex_cn: 他面临一个困境：是待在家里还是去上班。
words.en: A situation in which a difficult choice has to be made between two or more alternatives, especially equally undesirable ones.

words.tr:
n. 权宜之计；应急办法
adj. 权宜的
words.ex: Closing the factory was an expedient to save money.
words.ex_cn: 关闭工厂是为了省钱的权宜之计。
words.en: An expedient action or solution to a problem is one that is convenient or practical, although it may not be morally right.

words.tr:
adv. 光明正大地
adj. 光明正大的
words.ex: He always plays aboveboard in business.
words.ex_cn: 他在商业中总是光明正大。
words.en: If something is aboveboard, it is done in an honest and open way without any attempt to deceive.

words.tr: phrase. 主日学课程；在星期日学校中教授的宗教或道德教育课
words.ex: The child remembered his sunday-school lesson about kindness.
words.ex_cn: 这个孩子记得他关于善良的主日学课程。
words.en: A Sunday-school lesson is a class or session, typically for children, that teaches Christian principles and Bible stories, usually held on Sundays in a church.

words.ex: The team celebrated their triumph after winning the match.
words.ex_cn: 球队在赢得比赛后庆祝了他们的胜利。
words.en: A triumph is a great success or achievement, often one that has been gained with a lot of skill or effort.

words.ex: The hero will vanquish the dragon.
words.ex_cn: 英雄将战胜龙。
words.en: To vanquish someone means to defeat them completely in a battle or a competition.

words.tr: n. 企业家；创业者；承包人；
words.ex: He is an entrepreneur who started a small coffee shop.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位创办了小型咖啡店的企业家。
words.en: An entrepreneur is a person who organizes and operates a business or businesses, taking on greater than normal financial risks in order to do so.

words.tr:
v. （风）狂吹；咆哮；恫吓；咄咄逼人
n. 狂风声；咆哮；吓唬；夸口
words.ex: The wind blustered through the trees all night.
words.ex_cn: 风整晚狂吹着穿过树木。
words.en: If you say that someone is blustering, you mean that they are speaking aggressively but without authority, often because they are angry or offended.

words.ex: His story was an exaggeration of the truth.
words.ex_cn: 他的故事是对事实的夸张。
words.en: An exaggeration is a statement that represents something as better or worse than it really is.

words.tr:
n. 阶段；时期；
v. 分阶段进行；
words.ex: The project is in its final phase.
words.ex_cn: 这个项目正处于最后阶段。
words.en: A phase is a particular stage in a process or in the gradual development of something.

words.tr: adj. 不直接的；不正直的；迂回的；
words.ex: He gave a devious answer to avoid telling the truth.
words.ex_cn: 他给出了一个不直接的回答，以避免说出真相。
words.en: If you describe someone as devious, you mean that they are dishonest and unfair in the way that they behave, often by using indirect methods to achieve their aims.

words.ex: His hubris made him lose the game.
words.ex_cn: 他的傲慢让他输掉了比赛。
words.en: Hubris is excessive pride or self-confidence, often leading to downfall or failure.

words.ex: He bought an extravagant car that cost too much money.
words.ex_cn: 他买了一辆奢侈的车，价格太贵了。
words.en: Spending much more than is necessary or wise; excessively expensive.

words.ex: He had a stumble on the rocky path.
words.ex_cn: 他在布满石头的小路上绊了一跤。
words.en: To stumble means to trip or momentarily lose one's balance while walking or running. It can also refer to speaking in a hesitant or faltering manner.

words.ex: The witness lost credibility after lying.
words.ex_cn: 证人因撒谎而失去了可信性。
words.en: The quality of being trusted and believed in.

words.tr:
v. 渗出；流出；分泌出
n. 软泥；淤泥；泥浆
words.ex: Mud is oozing from the hole.
words.ex_cn: 泥巴正从洞里渗出来。
words.en: If a liquid oozes from something or if something oozes a liquid, the liquid flows from it slowly and in small quantities.

words.ex: The apple plummeted from the tree.
words.ex_cn: 苹果从树上垂直落下。
words.en: If an amount, rate, or price plummets, it decreases quickly by a large amount.

words.ex: She tried to prevail on him to change his mind.
words.ex_cn: 她试图劝服他改变主意。
words.en: If a proposal, principle, or opinion prevails, it gains influence or is accepted, often after a struggle or argument.

words.tr: vt. 提供资金；提供财务上的资助; n. 资金；钞票
words.ex: He bankrolled the new movie with his own money.
words.ex_cn: 他用自己的钱为这部新电影提供资金。
words.en: A bankroll is a sum of money that someone has available to spend, especially in a business context. To bankroll someone or something means to provide the money that they need for a particular project or activity.

words.tr: n. 流行行话；时髦词汇；
words.ex: The new app uses buzzwords like 'smart' and 'AI' to attract users.
words.ex_cn: 这款新应用使用了‘智能’和‘人工智能’等流行行话来吸引用户。
words.en: A buzzword is a word or phrase, often jargon, that becomes very popular for a period of time.

words.tr:
n. 袭击；罢工；
v. 击打；侵袭；突然想到；
words.ex: The strike on the base happened at dawn.
words.ex_cn: 对基地的袭击发生在黎明时分。
words.en: To hit someone or something forcefully; to stop work as a form of protest.

words.tr:
v. 扭动；摆动
n. 扭动；摆动
words.ex: The baby wiggles her toes when she laughs.
words.ex_cn: 当宝宝笑的时候，她会动动脚趾。
words.en: To move or cause to move up and down or from side to side with small rapid movements.

words.tr: n. 犬儒主义；愤世嫉俗；玩世不恭
words.ex: He showed cynicism about politicians' promises.
words.ex_cn: 他对政治家的承诺表现出愤世嫉俗。
words.en: Cynicism is the belief that people are motivated purely by self-interest rather than acting for honorable or unselfish reasons.

words.tr: n. 天花乱坠的广告宣传；炒作；
words.ex: The new phone got a lot of hype before its release.
words.ex_cn: 这款新手机在发布前受到了大量天花乱坠的广告宣传。
words.en: If someone or something is hyped, they are praised or advertised a lot in newspapers, on television, etc., especially in a way that is intended to make them seem very exciting or important.

words.tr: v. 以低于市价售出；抛售
words.ex: The store undersells other shops by lowering prices.
words.ex_cn: 这家商店通过降价来以低于市价售出商品。
words.en: To sell something at a lower price than competitors or to undervalue something.

words.ex: He uses optical lenses to see small objects.
words.ex_cn: 他使用光学镜片来看小物体。
words.en: Relating to sight, especially in relation to the physical action of light.

words.ex: The police tried to subdue the angry man.
words.ex_cn: 警察试图制服那个愤怒的人。
words.en: To subdue someone or something means to bring them under control by using force or persuasion.

words.tr: n. 参考；提及；介绍信；引用；
words.ex: Please use this book for reference.
words.ex_cn: 请使用这本书作为参考。
words.en: A reference is a mention of something or someone, or a letter or statement about someone's character or abilities.

words.ex: The health sector needs more funding.
words.ex_cn: 医疗部门需要更多资金。
words.en: A particular area of activity, especially one that is part of a larger area of activity or one that is considered separately from other areas.

words.tr: n. 落砂; 轻度经济衰退，股票市场震动; 摊平
words.ex: The shakeout removed sand from the metal casting.
words.ex_cn: 落砂去除了金属铸件中的砂子。
words.en: A competitive situation that eliminates weaker participants.

words.ex: He gave an explicit answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了明确的答案。
words.en: Something that is explicit is expressed or shown clearly and openly, without any attempt to hide anything.

words.tr: adj. 机会主义的；投机取巧的
words.ex: He is opportunistic and always takes advantage of easy chances.
words.ex_cn: 他很 opportunistic，总是抓住容易的机会。
words.en: If you describe someone's behaviour as opportunistic, you are critical of them because they take advantage of situations in order to gain money or power, without thinking about whether their actions are right or wrong.

words.tr:
v. 预备；准备
n. 家庭作业；预习功课
adj. 准备的
words.ex: He is preparing for the exam.
words.ex_cn: 他正在为考试做准备。
words.en: Preparation or preliminary work, especially in education or before an event.

words.ex: The two countries formed an alliance to fight the enemy.
words.ex_cn: 这两个国家结成联盟以对抗敌人。
words.en: An alliance is a group of countries or political parties that are formally united and working together because they have similar aims.

words.ex: He squeezed into the small seat.
words.ex_cn: 他挤进了小座位里。
words.en: To squeeze something means to press it firmly, usually with your fingers or hands, often to get liquid out of it or to make it smaller.

words.ex: The undercurrents of the river were strong and dangerous.
words.ex_cn: 河中的暗流强劲且危险。
words.en: An undercurrent is a current of water below the surface or an underlying feeling or influence, especially one that is hidden or not openly acknowledged.

words.ex: The razor-sharp knife cut the bread easily.
words.ex_cn: 那把刀刃锋利的刀轻松地切开了面包。
words.en: If you describe someone's intelligence, wit, or understanding as razor-sharp, you mean that it is extremely sharp, clear, and accurate.

words.ex: The judge was evenhanded in treating both sides.
words.ex_cn: 法官对双方都公平对待。
words.en: Treating everyone equally and fairly.

words.ex: The hawk made a sudden swoop to catch the mouse.
words.ex_cn: 老鹰突然俯冲下来抓老鼠。
words.en: To move very quickly and easily through the air, especially down from a height in order to attack.

words.ex: He bought a stake in the new company.
words.ex_cn: 他购买了这家新公司的股份。
words.en: A stake is a pointed stick or post that is pushed into the ground, for example to support a young tree. It can also refer to a share or interest in a business, situation, or system.

words.ex: The country made a unilateral decision to close the border.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家单方面决定关闭边境。
words.en: Involving only one group or country.

words.tr: n. （以金钱）赞助者；赛马的赌手
words.ex: The backer gave money to the new movie.
words.ex_cn: 赞助人给这部电影提供了资金。
words.en: A backer is someone who supports a project, organization, or person, often by giving money.

words.tr: n. 城河；壕坑; n. （Foss）人名；（德、英、法、西、瑞典）福斯
words.ex: The castle is surrounded by a deep foss.
words.ex_cn: 城堡被一条深城河环绕。
words.en: A fossilized remnant or trace of an organism from a past geological age.

words.ex: Her smile heartened the tired students.
words.ex_cn: 她的微笑鼓舞了疲惫的学生。
words.en: If someone is heartened by something, it encourages them and makes them cheerful.

words.ex: He is a maverick who always does things his own way.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个总是按自己方式做事的独行其是者。
words.en: If you describe someone as a maverick, you mean that they are unconventional and independent, and do not think or behave in the same way as other people.

words.tr: n. 无伤大雅的谎言，小谎；一击; vi. 撒小谎
words.ex: She told a fib about her age to get the job.
words.ex_cn: 她为了得到这份工作，撒了个关于年龄的小谎。
words.en: A fib is a small lie that is told to avoid hurting someone's feelings or to avoid a minor trouble.

words.ex: He was charged with perjury after lying in court.
words.ex_cn: 他在法庭上撒谎后被控伪证罪。
words.en: The crime of telling a lie in a court of law after having sworn to tell the truth.

words.tr: v. 使内在化；使成为自我之一部分
words.ex: Children often internalize the values and beliefs of their parents.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们常常将父母的价值观和信仰内在化。
words.en: If you internalize something such as a belief or a set of values, you make it become part of your attitude or way of thinking.

words.tr: adj. 明目张胆的；公然的；喧闹的
words.ex: He made a blatant lie to avoid punishment.
words.ex_cn: 他为了逃避惩罚，公然撒了谎。
words.en: If you describe an action as blatant, you mean that it is done in an open and obvious way, often with a lack of shame or embarrassment.

words.ex: The fabrication of the machine took three weeks.
words.ex_cn: 这台机器的制备花了三周时间。
words.en: The act of inventing or producing something false in order to deceive someone.

words.ex: Smoking is detrimental to your health.
words.ex_cn: 吸烟对你的健康有害。
words.en: Something that is detrimental has a harmful or damaging effect on something else.

words.ex: The children caused a big commotion in the classroom.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在教室里制造了很大的喧闹。
words.en: A commotion is a lot of noise, confusion, and excitement.

words.tr:
n. 回想
v. 回想
words.ex: In retrospect, I should have studied harder.
words.ex_cn: 回顾过去，我本该更努力学习的。
words.en: When you consider something in retrospect, you think about it afterwards, and often have a different opinion about it from the one that you had at the time.

words.ex: He listened to his conscience and told the truth.
words.ex_cn: 他听从了良心，说出了真相。
words.en: Your conscience is the part of your mind that tells you whether what you are doing is right or wrong.

words.tr:
n. 乳脂软糖；胡言
v. 敷衍；回避；捏造
words.ex: She made a fudge cake for the party.
words.ex_cn: 她为聚会做了一个乳脂软糖蛋糕。
words.en: If you fudge something, you avoid making a clear and definite decision, distinction, or statement about it.

words.tr:
n. 弯曲；曲线；
v. （使）弯成弧形；
words.ex: The road has a sharp curve ahead.
words.ex_cn: 前面的路有一个急转弯。
words.en: A curve is a smooth, gradually bending line, for example part of the edge of a circle.

words.ex: The proctor watched students during the exam.
words.ex_cn: 学监在考试期间监视学生。
words.en: A proctor is someone who supervises students during an examination to ensure that the rules are obeyed.

words.tr:
n. （一阵）剧痛；（一阵）不快
v. （使）感到一阵剧痛
words.ex: He felt a twinge in his leg after running.
words.ex_cn: 他跑步后腿里一阵刺痛。
words.en: A twinge is a sudden, sharp pain or emotion.

words.ex: He tried to justify his mistake by saying he was tired.
words.ex_cn: 他试图以自己累了为由来证明自己的错误是正当的。
words.en: To justify something means to show or prove that it is reasonable, necessary, or correct.

words.tr:
v. 告密；告发；偷窃
n. 告密者；告发者
words.ex: He was caught snitching money from the register.
words.ex_cn: 他因从收银机里偷钱被抓了。
words.en: To snitch means to secretly tell someone in authority that someone else has done something wrong, often in order to cause trouble for them. It can also mean to steal something, especially something small or not very valuable.

words.tr:
v. 使模糊；使看不清；弄污
n. 模糊
words.ex: The rain made the lights blur.
words.ex_cn: 雨使灯光变得模糊。
words.en: If something blurs your vision, it makes you unable to see things clearly.

words.tr: adj. 固有的；内在的；本身的；
words.ex: Honesty is an intrinsic part of her character.
words.ex_cn: 诚实是她性格中固有的部分。
words.en: belonging to a thing by its very nature

words.ex: He found himself in a predicament when he lost his wallet.
words.ex_cn: 当他丢掉钱包时，他陷入了困境。
words.en: A predicament is a difficult, perplexing, or trying situation.

words.ex: He has a scar on his arm from the accident.
words.ex_cn: 他手臂上有一道事故留下的伤疤。
words.en: A mark left on the skin after a wound or injury has healed, or the act of causing such a mark.
