words.tr: v. 使粉碎；使破碎；使破灭；
words.ex: The stone shattered when it hit the ground.
words.ex_cn: 石头撞到地面时碎裂了。
words.en: If something shatters or is shattered, it breaks into a lot of small pieces.

words.ex: The smell of flowers was pervasive in the garden.
words.ex_cn: 花的香味遍布整个花园。
words.en: Something that is pervasive is present or noticeable throughout a place or thing.

words.ex: He could discern a small bird in the trees.
words.ex_cn: 他能辨明树上有一只小鸟。
words.en: If you can discern something, you are aware of it and know what it is.

words.ex: He will partake in the school play.
words.ex_cn: 他将参与学校的戏剧表演。
words.en: To partake in something means to take part in or experience it.

words.tr: adj. 宽厚的；仁慈的；不严格的；
words.ex: The teacher was lenient with students who were late.
words.ex_cn: 老师对迟到的学生很宽厚。
words.en: If you are lenient with someone, you are not strict in the way you treat them, especially when they have done something wrong.

words.ex: He alleges that the manager stole money.
words.ex_cn: 他声称经理偷了钱。
words.en: If you allege that something bad is true, you say it but do not prove it.

words.ex: The guard showed vigilance during the night shift.
words.ex_cn: 守卫在夜班期间保持警惕。
words.en: Vigilance is the action or state of keeping careful watch for possible danger or difficulties.

words.ex: The bird hatched her eggs after three weeks.
words.ex_cn: 这只鸟在三周后孵出了她的蛋。
words.en: To hatch means to cause an egg to break open so that a young animal can come out, or to plan secretly with other people to do something bad or illegal.

words.tr:
adj. 狡猾的；奸诈的；巧妙的
n. 奸诈；狡猾
words.ex: The cunning fox tricked the chicken.
words.ex_cn: 那只狡猾的狐狸骗了鸡。
words.en: Someone who is cunning is clever and good at deceiving others in order to get what they want.

words.ex: He committed a transgression by stealing the money.
words.ex_cn: 他偷钱犯了过错。
words.en: A transgression is an act that goes against a law, rule, or code of conduct; an offense.

words.ex: Rain can hinder our plan to go hiking.
words.ex_cn: 雨天会妨碍我们去徒步旅行的计划。
words.en: If something hinders you, it makes it more difficult for you to do something or make progress.

words.ex: The twin boys are fraternal twins.
words.ex_cn: 这两个男孩是异卵双胞胎。
words.en: Fraternal is used to describe feelings or actions that are like those of a brother towards his brothers or sisters.

words.tr: adj. 蔓延的；杂乱无序伸展的； v. “sprawl”的现在分词；
words.ex: The sprawling city has many neighborhoods.
words.ex_cn: 这座蔓延的城市有许多社区。
words.en: If you describe something as sprawling, you mean that it covers a large area of land.

words.tr: phrase. 靠…茁壮；以…旺盛；喜欢
words.ex: Some people thrive on challenges and work better under pressure.
words.ex_cn: 有些人靠挑战成长，压力下工作得更好。
words.en: If someone thrives on a particular situation, they enjoy it or are successful in it.

words.tr: adj. 富有魅力的；迷人的；
words.ex: She wore a glamorous dress to the party.
words.ex_cn: 她穿了一条富有魅力的裙子去参加派对。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as glamorous, you mean that they are more attractive, exciting, or interesting than ordinary people or things.

words.tr: n. 副产品 ；让产易股；资产分派
words.ex: The movie was a spin-off of the popular TV series.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影是那部热门电视剧的副产品。
words.en: A spin-off is something that develops from something larger or more important, especially a television program or film that is based on a character or idea from an existing one.

words.tr:
v. 缓行；溜蹄
n. 溜蹄；缓行漫步
words.ex: He amble through the park after dinner.
words.ex_cn: 他晚饭后在公园里缓行。
words.en: To walk at a slow, relaxed pace, especially for pleasure.

words.ex: We walked along the coast and saw the sea.
words.ex_cn: 我们沿着海岸散步，看到了大海。
words.en: The coast is the land along the edge of the sea or ocean.

words.tr: n. 增援; 守场员; 外场手; 守场员（接手）的位置
words.ex: The fence is a backstop for the baseball field.
words.ex_cn: 这道围栏是棒球场的挡球网。
words.en: A backstop is something that provides support or acts as a last resort in case of failure.

words.ex: The car consumes a lot of gas.
words.ex_cn: 这辆车消耗很多汽油。
words.en: To consume something means to eat or drink it, or to use it up in some way.

words.ex: He laughed maniacally when he won the game.
words.ex_cn: 当他赢得比赛时，他疯狂地大笑。
words.en: In a manner that is extremely energetic, excited, or obsessive.

words.tr: adj. 讲究实际的；头脑清晰的；不感情用事的
words.ex: He is hardheaded and won't change his mind.
words.ex_cn: 他很固执，不会改变主意。
words.en: If you describe someone as hardheaded, you mean that they are practical and determined to get what they want, and do not let emotions or other people's opinions affect them.

words.tr: v. 熄灭；平息；抑制（欲望）；用水冷却
words.ex: He quenched the fire with water.
words.ex_cn: 他用水熄灭了火。
words.en: To satisfy one's thirst or to extinguish a fire or to suppress a feeling or desire.

words.tr: phrase. 引燃火；长明火；指示灯（用于点燃主燃烧器的小火焰或指示设备状态的小灯）
words.ex: The pilot light on the stove is still burning.
words.ex_cn: 炉子上的长明火还在燃烧。
words.en: A small flame that is kept alight to ignite a gas burner.

words.ex: He has a gene that makes him tall.
words.ex_cn: 他有一个让他长高的基因。
words.en: A gene is the basic physical and functional unit of heredity. Genes, which are made up of DNA, act as instructions to make molecules called proteins.

words.ex: He showed his portfolio to the art teacher.
words.ex_cn: 他向美术老师展示了他作品集。
words.en: A portfolio is a set of pictures by someone, or photographs of examples of their work, which they use when entering competitions or applying for work.

words.tr: phrase. 零和博弈；零和游戏（一方所得即为另一方所失，总和为零）
words.ex: The match is a zero-sum game: one team wins, and the other loses.
words.ex_cn: 这场比赛是零和博弈：一方赢，另一方输。
words.en: A situation in which one person's gain is equivalent to another's loss, so the net change in wealth or benefit is zero.

words.ex: The buffalo walks slowly across the grassland.
words.ex_cn: 水牛缓慢地走过草原。
words.en: A buffalo is a large animal of the cattle family, with long, curved horns. In North America, the buffalo is also called the bison.

words.ex: He punches out at 5 p.m. every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天下午五点打卡下班。
words.en: To record the time of one's departure from work by punching a time clock; to hit someone or something with a fist.

words.ex: He is manifestly wrong about the answer.
words.ex_cn: 他关于这个答案显然是错的。
words.en: In a way that is clear or obvious to the eye or mind.

words.ex: The anthropologist studies ancient tribes.
words.ex_cn: 这位人类学家研究古代部落。
words.en: An anthropologist is a person who studies anthropology, which is the study of human societies and cultures and their development.

words.ex: His eccentricity makes him unique.
words.ex_cn: 他的古怪使他与众不同。
words.en: The quality of being eccentric; behaviour that is unusual, peculiar, or odd.

words.tr:
n. 扑鼠器
v. 诱捕
words.ex: He set a mousetrap in the kitchen.
words.ex_cn: 他在厨房里设了一个捕鼠器。
words.en: A device for catching and usually killing mice, typically baited with food.

words.tr: v. 驱散；消散；浪费；挥霍
words.ex: The fog will dissipate by noon.
words.ex_cn: 雾将在中午前消散。
words.en: If something dissipates or is dissipated, it becomes less or becomes less strong until it disappears or goes away completely.

words.tr: adj. 散漫的；不连贯的；断续的
words.ex: He gave a desultory answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了一个漫无目的的回答。
words.en: Something that is desultory is done in an unplanned and disorganized way, and without enthusiasm.

words.ex: The baby smiled at the sweet melody.
words.ex_cn: 宝宝听到了甜美的旋律，笑了。
words.en: A melody is a sequence of single notes that is musically satisfying.

words.tr:
n. 旷野地；荒野；高沼
v. （使）停泊；系泊
words.ex: The sheep graze on the moor near the village.
words.ex_cn: 羊在村庄附近的旷野地上吃草。
words.en: A moor is an area of open land, often with poor soil, that is covered with grass, heather, and low bushes. It can also refer to the act of securing a ship or boat to a fixed object or the land.

words.tr: n. 精疲力竭；过度劳累
words.ex: He feels burnout after working too many hours.
words.ex_cn: 他工作太久后感到精疲力尽。
words.en: Burnout is a state of emotional, physical, and mental exhaustion caused by excessive and prolonged stress. It occurs when you feel overwhelmed, emotionally drained, and unable to meet constant demands.

words.tr: n. 实习工作；安排；放置；
words.ex: He got a placement at a local company this summer.
words.ex_cn: 他今年夏天获得了一份在本地公司的实习工作。
words.en: The act of placing something or someone in a particular position or the process of finding a suitable place or job for someone.

words.ex: The pup played with a ball in the yard.
words.ex_cn: 小狗在院子里玩球。
words.en: A pup is a young dog.

words.ex: She is weaning her baby off milk.
words.ex_cn: 她正在让宝宝戒掉牛奶。
words.en: To wean someone off something means to make them gradually stop using or depending on it, especially something harmful or unnecessary.

words.tr: phrase. 领头狼；狼群中的首领个体
words.ex: The alpha wolf leads the pack.
words.ex_cn: 头狼带领狼群。
words.en: The alpha wolf is the leader of a wolf pack, usually the strongest and most dominant male or female, responsible for making decisions for the pack's welfare.

words.tr:
n. 老家伙；老朽
adj. 老年病学的；老年医学的
words.ex: The geriatric patient needs help walking.
words.ex_cn: 这位老年病人需要帮助走路。
words.en: Geriatric refers to the branch of medicine or social science dealing with the health and care of old people.

words.tr: adj. 喜怒无常的；性情的；易兴奋的
words.ex: She is known for her temperamental nature, often changing moods without warning.
words.ex_cn: 她以喜怒无常著称，常常毫无预警地改变情绪。
words.en: If you say that someone is temperamental, you are criticizing them for not being calm or reliable, but tending to have sudden changes of mood or behavior.

words.ex: He is phlegmatic even when things go wrong.
words.ex_cn: 即使事情出错，他依然冷静。
words.en: A phlegmatic person does not usually get emotional or excited about things.

words.ex: He must bestir himself to finish the work.
words.ex_cn: 他必须振作起来完成这项工作。
words.en: To rouse to action; to make active or alert.

words.ex: The graph has a cusp at x = 0.
words.ex_cn: 这个图像在 x = 0 处有一个尖点。
words.en: The point of intersection of two curves or the pointed end of something.

words.ex: He used a template to write the report.
words.ex_cn: 他用了一个模板来写报告。
words.en: A template is a thin sheet of plastic or metal in a particular shape, used in drawing shapes or cutting materials accurately.

words.ex: This car needs high octane fuel.
words.ex_cn: 这辆车需要高辛烷值汽油。
words.en: A hydrocarbon of the alkane series, used as a fuel and solvent.

words.tr:
adj. 无法精确估量的
n. 无法估量的事物
words.ex: The reason for his silence is imponderable.
words.ex_cn: 他沉默的原因无法衡量。
words.en: An imponderable factor or element is one that cannot be precisely measured or assessed.

words.ex: The primal forest has never been touched by humans.
words.ex_cn: 这片原始森林从未被人类触碰过。
words.en: Primal means relating to an early stage in the development of something, or being the most important or basic part of something.

words.ex: He used a thin wire to fix the broken hook.
words.ex_cn: 他用一根细金属丝固定了坏掉的钩子。
words.en: A wire is a long thin piece of metal that is used to fasten things or to carry electric current.

words.tr:
v. 拼写；意味着；
n. 一段时间；
words.ex: Can you spell your name?
words.ex_cn: 你能拼出你的名字吗？
words.en: If you spell a word, you write or speak each letter in the correct order.

words.ex: The earthquake was a catastrophe.
words.ex_cn: 这场地震是一场灾难。
words.en: An event causing great and often sudden damage or suffering; a disaster.

words.ex: This color befits the room.
words.ex_cn: 这个颜色适合这个房间。
words.en: To be suitable or appropriate for someone or something.

words.ex: The school's ethos is respect for everyone.
words.ex_cn: 这所学校的社會精神特质是尊重每一个人。
words.en: The fundamental character or spirit of a culture; the underlying sentiment that informs the beliefs, customs, or practices of a group or society.

words.ex: The store gave us a freebie with our purchase.
words.ex_cn: 商店在我们购买时送了我们一件免费赠品。
words.en: A freebie is something that is given to you without you having to pay for it.

words.ex: He etches a design on the glass.
words.ex_cn: 他在玻璃上刻了一个图案。
words.en: To etch means to cut into a surface, especially metal or glass, using acid or a sharp tool, in order to create a design or pattern.

words.ex: He acted on impulse and bought the car.
words.ex_cn: 他一时冲动买了那辆车。
words.en: An impulse is a sudden strong desire to do something without thinking about the consequences.

words.tr: n. 轻易放弃的人；半途而废者
words.ex: He was labeled a quitter after he dropped out of the marathon.
words.ex_cn: 他在马拉松比赛中途退出后，被贴上了半途而废者的标签。
words.en: A quitter is someone who gives up easily and does not finish something they have started.

words.ex: He shouted with fury when he lost the game.
words.ex_cn: 当他输掉比赛时，他愤怒地大喊。
words.en: Fury is a feeling of intense anger.

words.ex: He will tackle the problem tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他明天会处理这个问题。
words.en: If you tackle a problem or task, you deal with it in a determined way. In sports such as football and rugby, a tackle is an act of trying to take the ball from a player on the other team.

words.tr: phrase. 木头上的一个凸起；比喻毫无作用或毫无生气的人或事物
words.ex: He sat there like a bump on a log, saying nothing.
words.ex_cn: 他坐在那里一动不动，什么也没说。
words.en: Someone who is dull, uninteresting, or does nothing to contribute.

words.tr:
n. 猎犬
v. 追逐；纠缠
words.ex: The hound chased the rabbit through the forest.
words.ex_cn: 猎犬在森林里追赶兔子。
words.en: A hound is a type of dog used for hunting or chasing. It can also refer to someone who persistently pursues or bothers someone else.

words.tr:
n. 嘲笑；嘲弄
v. 嘲笑；狼吞虎咽
words.ex: His joke received a scoff from the crowd.
words.ex_cn: 他的笑话引来了人群的嘲笑。
words.en: If you scoff at something, you speak about it in a way that shows you think it is ridiculous or inadequate.

words.tr: adj. 庸俗的；粗俗的；粗野的；下流的
words.ex: He used a vulgar word in class.
words.ex_cn: 他在课堂上说了一个粗俗的词。
words.en: If you describe something as vulgar, you mean that it is in bad taste or of poor quality.

words.tr: adj. 结核的；[医] 结节的；瘤状的
words.ex: The patient has a tubercular infection in the lung.
words.ex_cn: 这位病人的肺部有结核感染。
words.en: Relating to or affected by tuberculosis, a serious infectious disease that can affect many parts of the body, especially the lungs.

words.ex: The wound caused a serious infection.
words.ex_cn: 伤口引起了严重的感染。
words.en: An infection is a disease caused by microorganisms such as bacteria, viruses, or parasites invading the body.

words.tr: adj. 自杀的；有自杀倾向的；有致命危险的
words.ex: He felt suicidal after losing his job.
words.ex_cn: 他失业后感到想自杀。
words.en: If someone is suicidal, they are likely to try to kill themselves.

words.tr: v. 使制度化或习俗化；使送进专门机构
words.ex: The government wants to institutionalize the new policy.
words.ex_cn: 政府希望将这项新政策制度化。
words.en: To institutionalize something means to make it a fixed and accepted part of a system, organization, or society.

words.ex: He planted carrots in a small patch.
words.ex_cn: 他在一小块地上种了胡萝卜。
words.en: A patch is a piece of material used to mend a hole or a weak spot in something, or a small area that is different from the area around it.

words.tr: n. 工作服；罩衫；宽松式衬衫
words.ex: The painter wore a smock to protect his clothes.
words.ex_cn: 画家穿了一件工作服来保护他的衣服。
words.en: A smock is a loose garment worn over clothes to protect them while working or doing messy tasks.

words.ex: The war impoverished many families.
words.ex_cn: 这场战争使许多家庭变得贫困。
words.en: To make someone poor or to reduce the quality, strength, or richness of something.

words.ex: She invited all her kin to the family reunion.
words.ex_cn: 她邀请了所有亲属参加家庭聚会。
words.en: Your kin are your relatives.

words.tr:
v. 目瞪口呆地看；裂开
n. 目瞪口呆地看；裂口
words.ex: The children gape at the magic show.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们张大嘴看着魔术表演。
words.en: To open the mouth wide; to stare with open mouth, as in wonder.

words.ex: The cloud floats high in the sky.
words.ex_cn: 云朵在天空中飘浮。
words.en: A cloud is a visible mass of condensed water vapor floating in the atmosphere, typically high above the ground.

words.tr: phrase. 舔食；欣然接受；迫不及待地吸收（信息等）
words.ex: The dog will lap up all the milk.
words.ex_cn: 狗会把所有的牛奶舔干净。
words.en: To accept or absorb something eagerly or with great enthusiasm.

words.ex: The monster made a monstrous sound.
words.ex_cn: 这个怪物发出了巨大的声音。
words.en: If you describe something as monstrous, you mean that it is extremely large or that it is extremely unpleasant or wrong.

words.ex: The weather today is dreadful.
words.ex_cn: 今天的天气令人不快。
words.en: If you say that something is dreadful, you mean that it is very bad or unpleasant, or very poor in quality.

words.tr: adj. 丑恶的；可怕的；丑陋的；
words.ex: The monster had a hideous face.
words.ex_cn: 这个怪物有一张丑恶的脸。
words.en: If you say that someone or something is hideous, you mean that they are very ugly or unattractive.

words.ex: The butchery of innocent people shocked the world.
words.ex_cn: 对无辜者的屠杀震惊了世界。
words.en: The business or work of slaughtering animals and preparing them for sale as meat; a place where this is done; also, the cruel and unnecessary killing of people.

words.ex: I sympathize with people who are hungry.
words.ex_cn: 我同情那些挨饿的人。
words.en: If you sympathize with someone who is in a bad situation, you feel sorry for them.

words.tr: phrase. 因骄傲而自大；洋洋得意；趾高气扬
words.ex: He was puffed up with pride after winning the race.
words.ex_cn: 他赢得比赛后得意洋洋。
words.en: To be excessively proud or arrogant.

words.ex: He always follows the maxim 'work hard, play hard'.
words.ex_cn: 他总是遵循‘努力工作，尽情玩耍’这一信条。
words.en: A maxim is a short, easily remembered expression of a basic principle, general truth, or rule of conduct.

words.ex: The clown entertains the children with funny tricks.
words.ex_cn: 小丑用滑稽的把戏娱乐孩子们。
words.en: To entertain someone means to amuse or interest them, for example by telling them stories or jokes, or by playing music for them.

words.ex: He wanted vengeance after his brother was hurt.
words.ex_cn: 他哥哥被伤害后，他想要报复。
words.en: Vengeance is the act of doing something harmful or unpleasant to someone because they have done something harmful or unpleasant to you.

words.ex: The room was decorated with gaudy colors that hurt the eyes.
words.ex_cn: 房间用俗丽的颜色装饰，刺眼。
words.en: If you describe something as gaudy, you mean that it is very brightly coloured and showy, but not in an attractive way.

words.tr:
n. 滑稽模仿；讽刺作品
adj. 滑稽模仿的；讽刺性作品的
v. 模仿嘲弄
words.ex: The burlesque show was a hit with the audience.
words.ex_cn: 滑稽讽刺表演受到了观众的热烈欢迎。
words.en: A burlesque is a performance or a piece of writing that makes fun of something or someone by copying them in an exaggerated way.

words.tr: phrase. 估量某人；打量某人（以判断其性格、能力或意图）
words.ex: He sized me up when I walked into the room.
words.ex_cn: 我走进房间时，他打量了我一番。
words.en: To estimate or judge someone's abilities or character.

words.ex: The boy fixed the circuitry in his toy car.
words.ex_cn: 男孩修好了他玩具车里的电路。
words.en: The interconnected system of circuits in a device or system, especially in electronics.

words.tr:
n. 倒塌；崩溃；暴跌；
v. 倒塌；崩溃；
words.ex: The collapse of the old bridge caused many problems.
words.ex_cn: 这座旧桥的倒塌引起了诸多问题。
words.en: If a building or other structure collapses, it falls down very suddenly.

words.tr: phrasal verb. 开始认真对待某事，集中精力努力工作
words.ex: He must buckle down to finish his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他必须专心完成作业。
words.en: If you buckle down to something, you start working seriously at it.

words.ex: His idiotic comments made everyone laugh.
words.ex_cn: 他那些愚蠢的评论让大家都笑了。
words.en: If you call someone or something idiotic, you mean that they are very stupid or silly.

words.tr: phrase. 激烈的竞争；永无休止的奔忙；内卷式职场生活
words.ex: He left the rat race to live a quiet life.
words.ex_cn: 他离开了竞争激烈的生活，过上了宁静的生活。
words.en: A rat race is an endless, self-defeating, or pointless pursuit. It conjures up the image of the futile efforts of a lab rat trying to escape while running around a maze or in a wheel.

words.tr:
v. 使腐败；
adj. 腐败的；
words.ex: The official was corrupt by taking bribes.
words.ex_cn: 这位官员因收受贿赂而腐败。
words.en: If someone is corrupt, they do things that are dishonest or illegal in order to gain money or power.

words.ex: They exalt their hero with cheers.
words.ex_cn: 他们用欢呼赞美他们的英雄。
words.en: To exalt someone or something means to praise them very highly.

words.ex: He waits for the gratification of winning the game.
words.ex_cn: 他等待赢得比赛的满足感。
words.en: Gratification is the pleasure or satisfaction you feel when you get something you wanted or worked for.

words.tr: phrase. 听任；甘心接受；使自己顺从于
words.ex: He resigns himself to the fact that change takes time.
words.ex_cn: 他只好接受改变需要时间这一事实。
words.en: To accept something unpleasant that one cannot do anything about.

words.ex: He wants to change the status quo.
words.ex_cn: 他想改变现状。
words.en: The status quo is the state of affairs that exists at a particular time, especially in contrast to a different possible state of affairs.

words.ex: It's preposterous to think cats can drive cars.
words.ex_cn: 认为猫会开车是极其荒谬的。
words.en: If you describe something as preposterous, you mean that it is extremely unreasonable and foolish.

words.ex: He finally conceded defeat after the match.
words.ex_cn: 比赛结束后，他终于承认失败了。
words.en: If you concede something, you admit, often unwillingly, that it is true or correct.

words.ex: The sandpaper feels coarse to the touch.
words.ex_cn: 这张砂纸摸起来很粗糙。
words.en: Coarse things have a rough texture because they consist of thick threads or large pieces.

words.ex: The defect in the phone made it hard to use.
words.ex_cn: 手机的缺陷让它很难使用。
words.en: A defect is a fault or imperfection in a person or thing.

words.ex: His views were considered heretical by the religious authorities.
words.ex_cn: 他的观点被宗教权威认为是异端的。
words.en: If someone's beliefs or actions are heretical, they are contrary to the official or accepted beliefs or practices of a particular religion or group.

words.tr: 短语动词. 意味着；相当于；总计达到
words.ex: His debts amount to over $50,000.
words.ex_cn: 他的债务总计超过5万美元。
words.en: If something amounts to a particular total, all the parts of it add up to that total.

words.ex: He drinks a martini after work.
words.ex_cn: 他下班后喝一杯马提尼。
words.en: A martini is a cocktail made with gin and vermouth, and often garnished with an olive or a lemon twist.

words.ex: He drinks gin with ice.
words.ex_cn: 他喝加冰的杜松子酒。
words.en: A clear strong alcoholic drink flavoured with juniper berries.

words.tr: adj. 无望的；凄凉的；荒凉的；
words.ex: The future looks bleak without a job.
words.ex_cn: 没有工作，未来看起来毫无希望。
words.en: If you describe a situation as bleak, you mean that it seems unlikely to improve or get better.

words.ex: The dark clouds forebode a storm.
words.ex_cn: 乌云预示着一场风暴。
words.en: If something forebodes a future event, it suggests that it is going to happen.

words.ex: The drumbeat echoed through the night.
words.ex_cn: 鼓声在夜晚回荡。
words.en: A drumbeat is the sound of a drum being hit, or a strong, continuous effort to support or promote something.
